pages.html:
Native capability coverage — CyTools_Subtitle 0.7.0#

Inventory source: fermion-research 0.2.14 installed CLI help, fermion/_speech engine implementation, https://github.com/fermionresearch/phonon/blob/main/docs/cli.md and https://www.fermionresearch.com/docs/speech/. Scope: local file transcription and subtitle authoring. Status below distinguishes actual execution from available code.

Native capability Tool operation/field Standalone Evidence / status
Phonon-2 word-timed English transcribe.model=phonon-2 Model + Generate Real English audio, segmented 5 s windows; real video through MCP
Phonon-2.5 multilingual transcribe.model=phonon-2.5 Model + Generate Real French audio, 8 s windows, accents preserved
Phonon-2.5 English variant transcribe.model=phonon-2.5-en Model selection/install Implemented, no separate inference run
Local compatible directory transcribe.local_model, register_local_model Local folder / Register / select SHA256 + architecture-family validation; fixture tested
CPU and native thread kernels device=cpu, threads CPU threads Actual engine=cpu in reports, non-default 2 threads tested
CUDA container / MLX engines Unavailable No GPU option Excluded: no container ownership or Apple hardware integration in this Tool
Word and segment times / --json transcribe outputs words/cues Player and editor Actual decoder timing; no invented uniform word timestamps
CPU --threads threads 1..32 Slider Passed into native CLI; real non-default value tested
--hotwords / --hotword-lambda hotwords array / hotword_lambda Vocabulary and strength Real French + video jobs with non-default vocabulary/strength
--hotwords-file / repeated flags Serialized hotwords array Same vocabulary form Equivalent terms, excludes arbitrary @FILE indirection
--hotword-strength Unavailable None Phonon-1 option; Phonon-1 excluded because it has no word timestamps
--download-only / repair install_model Installation Both actual requested models downloaded; upstream archive pins + local container SHA256
--verbose / timings Worker diagnostics + chunk metadata Application log Raw third-party diagnostics retained, no fake token streaming
Greedy decoding / no samplers Fixed native behavior No sampler controls Native engine has no transcription temperature/top-p knobs
Native long-file windows Outer bounded sequential windows Window / overlap sliders 5 s and 8 s tests; absolute word timing restored using offsets; midpoint ownership
Audio input formats media automatic import + FFmpeg PCM conversion File picker/path WAV and MP4 actual runs; other suffixes depend on installed FFmpeg and are unvalidated individually
Multitrack source audio_stream ordinal Audio-track slider Passed to FFmpeg; non-default track test documented in test suite
Live microphone / listen / server Unavailable None Outside local file subtitle task; SDK already supplies authenticated MCP/HTTP
Native bench / CPU describe Not business operations Logs / dependency status Excluded from subtitle jobs; administrative benchmark not required for subtitle generation
LoRA / generic arbitrary models Unavailable Explicit explanation Engine has no generic LoRA support; compatible directories only
Vocal source separation Not claimed Voice filter label Implemented FFT denoise + bandpass, no neural separator model
Sound classification / descriptions Reviewer edits, kind=sound Add sound description MCP sound edit tested. Native Phonon cannot identify non-speech events; inspect excerpt for external listening/classification
Forced alignment of arbitrary script Not claimed Cue text/start/end and shift Manual/MCP retiming and original-word reflow available; no aligner model supplied
Translation Unavailable None No translation model integrated

All business fields and invocation envelopes are exposed through Advanced operations. The simplified form additionally provides the common controls. Schema field count is not a claim of universal native capability coverage. JSON/SRT/VTT outputs are private, composable artifacts; MIME types and seconds units are declared in the manifest. Every input-file field is configured for task-owned automatic import. Model references and export destinations are not task inputs.

0.2.0 adds Tool-owned timing repair, not a new Phonon model capability: repair_subtitles, automatic transcription/reflow postprocessing, bounded early/late shifts, reading speed, short-fragment merging and persistent anchors. The editor and MCP use the same isolated worker. Native words, sound captions and manual speech edits are retained; warnings that cannot be resolved within the bounds remain visible. Tested on a complete 58m56s French recording through MCP, with exact word/text preservation and task export/cleanup checks.

Optional inference runtime in 0.3.0#

Capability Operation Standalone Contract
PyTorch availability without importing the engine runtime_status Installation state / Check PyTorch installation Installed/Missing, expected and detected package versions
Private CPU dependency installation install_runtime License review / Download or repair PyTorch Authenticated network permission; license_accepted, repair; fixed package pins, verified candidate activation

PyTorch and its specific math dependencies are absent from the Windows base archive. Model installation and optional runtime installation remain separate operations. Linux/macOS installation is not validated. See RuntimeInstallation.md and Validation.md.

Optional Community-1 speaker analysis (0.5.0)#

Native inventory: pyannote.audio 4.0.7 Pipeline.from_pretrained and SpeakerDiarization.apply signatures, packaged upstream sources and the official Community-1 model card. CPU PyTorch 2.8.0+cpu and torchaudio 2.8.0+cpu live in an isolated optional component; Phonon's runtime is unchanged.

Native capability Tool operation / fields Standalone Validation
Global speaker and exclusive timelines transcribe.diarization, diarize_subtitles Generation toggle / Speakers Real CPU inference: one voice and four alternating turns with two synthetic voices; automatic count
Known count / count bounds speaker_count, min_speakers, max_speakers Speaker analysis settings Schema bounds and argument construction
Segmentation / embedding batches segmentation_batch_size, embedding_batch_size Speaker analysis settings Applied in real CPU pipeline runs
CPU threads threads Existing threads setting Applied to optional PyTorch worker
Local checkpoint / offline inference register_diarization_model; managed pinned model Installation / local folder Restricted config paths and SHA256 checks
Credentials / gated download check_diarization_access, install_diarization_model Protected token field / official conditions link Real gated HTTP refusal, no token in business schema
Runtime installation install_diarization_runtime License review / install Real hashed wheel installation and CPU import verified
Manual voice/name corrections edit_subtitles speaker, rename_speakers Cue speaker / names Real runtime and GUI jobs, export and cleanup
Progress callback No arbitrary callable input Existing jobs/logs Worker phase and native logs; not fabricated per-batch percentages
GPU / multi-GPU Excluded for Community-1 CPU explicitly shown NVIDIA CUDA uses a separate engine below
Training, custom classes, biometric embeddings Excluded None Outside file subtitle attribution; no arbitrary Python classes or code parameters

All options are available in Advanced operations and generation configurations. Raw words and manual caption text are not overwritten by speaker attribution; explicit reflow/rebuild keeps its documented replacement behavior.

Optional NVIDIA Nemotron 3 (0.6.0)#

Inventory: official NeMo-Speech.cpp v0.2.0 CLI help/configuration and native diarization source, plus NVIDIA's Nemotron-3-Diarization model card. Only its pinned Windows CPU/CUDA diarization path is integrated; this is not NVIDIA speech transcription.

Native capability Operation / fields Standalone Evidence
Q8_0 Sortformer global activity diarization_engine=nemotron3 Engine selector Same natural capture, CPU/CUDA/full runs
CPU / CUDA:0 nemotron_device Device selector Native doctor and actual result device; no silent fallback
Streaming quality / low latency / full attention nemotron_mode, nemotron_preset Speaker settings Chunked and full executed; full limited to 360 s
Custom cache/context geometry nemotron_chunk/right_context/left_context/fifo/spkcache/update_period Custom preset fields Real custom preset run, exact CLI forwarding and compatibility checks
Activity thresholds and durations nemotron_onset/offset/pad_onset/pad_offset/min_duration_on/min_duration_off Advanced segmentation fields Real nondefault thresholds/zero padding run; native flags
CPU resource cap threads CPU threads Worker affinity inherited by real native child
Automatic speaker count, up to eight Fixed native behavior Explained in form Count/batch overrides for Community-1 rejected
Overlapping activity Raw segments + derived exclusiveSegments Reviewable cue candidates Overlap regression test; derived policy recorded
Verified runtime/model install, local reference install_nemotron_*, register_nemotron_model Installation Both runtimes and model installed through authenticated operations
Hardware diagnostics nemotron_diagnostics Check selected runtime Actual compatible GPU detected
Device memory, lifecycle SDK reservations, ProcessWorker Existing jobs/cancel CUDA reservation and real native-child cancellation check
Other native ASR/translation/server functions Excluded None Outside this optional voice-attribution component

The same public schemas serve MCP and desktop. Run-time diagnostics, immutable words, renamed/manual voices, exports and task cleanup use the existing composable document contract. See NVIDIA guide.

Modular interface (0.7.0)#

Core, Timeline, Inspector, Images, Diagnostics, Commands and Code/Python CodeEditor replace the covered local presentation. Canvas is their selected dependency. Engine decoding, validation, job operations and Undo history remain application-owned. No new model capability or platform support is declared. See CyUIMigration.md for the exact selection and validation evidence.

pages.title: Modular CyUI interface — 0.7.0
pages.html:
Modular CyUI interface — 0.7.0#

CyTools_Subtitle uses the unmodified Python implementation of CyUI 1.2.0, revision ff023e646c6a3038b3dfbfd53f6d2b4a2f5955e3. The previous application state is retained in local checkpoint 52980f1 (parent 3a08752). No SDK/model/runtime migration is required.

Modules and ownership#

Selected family Application use Replaced presentation
Core Shell, palette, fonts, widgets, notifications, EN/FR localization Older patched CyUI file and duplicated label/translation identity implementation
Timeline Speech, speaker and sound lanes; ruler seeking, range selection, zoom/pan, move/trim, Delete Subtitle playback slider; adds direct caption timing gestures
Inspector Typed start/end/text/type drafts, validation and cancellation Individual hand-built caption property fields
Images GPU video texture surface with fit, pointer zoom and pan immvision image widget and local aspect-fit canvas
Diagnostics Bounded cached log rows, filters, severity, follow, row selection, copy visible Local full-file-only log presentation
Commands Ctrl+Shift+P palette, keyboard navigation and disabled actions Centralizes access to existing file/playback/view/history actions
Code / Python CodeEditor Searchable syntax views for contracts/results; JSON editing and native text Undo Plain JSON multiline readers/editors
Canvas Automatic dependency of Timeline and Images Shared clipping and coordinate/navigation surface

Only 13 required Python source files are vendored in app/cyui.py and app/cyui_modules. Each is byte-checked against cyui-source.json. No Audio, AudioViews, Plots, Curves, Nodes, Diff, Assets, Viewport, DocumentViews, Gallery, Web or CEF module is shipped. Playback uses the existing application decoder/audio engine; this product had no waveform/spectrum/DSP editor to migrate. The static caption list and model/provider installation forms remain application-specific data views using Core widgets. There is no Web/Unreal integration.

Read-only JSON views retain a Selectable JSON text mode for partial selection/copy in addition to full-copy actions. Python CodeEditor uses the common ImGui multiline editor plus syntax preview; it does not expose the C++ TextEditor multiple-cursor/completion backend. No native Lexilla, CEF, TextEditor, Audio/Gallery library, NumPy replacement, OpenGL package or second Dear ImGui instance is added. The one imgui-bundle 1.93.0 renderer and existing media dependencies remain pinned. This Python host has no CyUI CMake target; CYUI_MODULES/CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET apply to native consumers, not this adapter. The Windows launcher remains a small C++17 program.

Reproduce and verify the integration#

powershell
.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app/sync_cyui.py --check# Restore the exact selected blobs from a local checkout containing the pinned commit:.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app/sync_cyui.py --sync --source PATH_TO_CYUI.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest app/test_modular_ui.py -q

The sync tool reads committed Git blobs without modifying the reference checkout, rejects hash changes and verifies selected Python import dependencies. It performs no automatic network fetch or install. .gitattributes preserves LF bytes for the vendored snapshot. To update CyUI deliberately, review the new revision/modules, update the pins and rerun the same checks. Do not patch copied library files; application adapters belong in subtitle_ui.py. Existing source/portable builders include the selected source package and complete CyUI MIT notice in root/app LICENCES.

Compile the launcher with app/build_launcher.ps1 in an x64 MSVC developer environment. Build a fresh Windows base with app/build_windows.py, validate the resulting directory, then package it using --package-only. Existing Python/media dependencies are unchanged. App update archives can carry this migration under the existing runtime ABI; installation data, models and optional engines remain separate.

Transactions, identity and review#

Each timeline has independent state and stable nonzero uint64 IDs derived from the document's string cue/speaker IDs. Label changes never change identity. The Tool retains original string IDs in JSON/MCP. Visible clip sets are indexed/cached by document revision; a range containing more than 3,000 visible captions prompts zooming rather than silently dropping data. Full text remains available in the caption list/inspector. Clip labels use Core's clipping helper.

Timeline begin/update events are previews. Only commit sends one existing edit_subtitles operation for the entire gesture, after domain validation. Escape or a revision/view change cancels previews. Invalid or negative timing rejects the complete proposal. Moving between voice/sound lanes makes an explicit speaker/type patch; same-lane timing edits preserve text, original words, sound descriptions and voice metadata. Original media/documents are never overwritten.

Inspector edits remain drafts until Apply cue edit. Native text Undo belongs to that focused field. Invalid drafts do not enable Apply. Outside text input, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z) traverse application-owned retained document versions; a completed gesture is one history step. History is bounded to 40 versions / 32 MiB (the current document is always retained). A no-op Save changes the exportable bundle without adding a spurious Undo step. Undo/Redo retain the matching output job, so export uses the selected version. A late correction result remains saved but does not replace a different document opened while it ran.

File rotation/discovery, redaction, authenticated job events and full-log reading remain in standalone_log.py. Diagnostics supplies rows/filter/follow/copy-visible. The app retains Copy entire log and a selectable raw-text section; refresh pauses while selecting raw text. Video decoding stays bounded/off the UI thread. The UI uploads/retires GPU textures and releases them before renderer shutdown. Images supplies fit/zoom/pan; subtitle overlays remain domain presentation using palette/dp.

English remains the default; French selection persists. Application catalogs are registered with the common CyUI locale API. User text, names, paths, IDs and protocol values are never translated. All dimensions/colors in the adapters use CyUI metrics/roles. Existing configuration callbacks, optional engine installation, GPU selection, exports and MCP operations are retained.

Verification#

Windows x64: 86 tests pass, including real ImGui move/trim/commit/cancel/revision gestures, typed-field cancellation, keyboard command execution, stable language IDs, snapshot hashes/import closure, atomic patches, history branching/budgets and unchanged word evidence. Existing preview, timing, diarization, security/resource and configuration tests remain in the suite.

The actual EXE rendered all eight views in English and French across five themes and both densities. A synthetic padded-width video and subtitle document exercised the texture surface and a real edit job followed by Undo/Redo. Headless ImGui frames also rendered adapters at 100%, 125%, 150% and 200% style DPI. This does not certify moving a native window between physical monitors. The rebuilt native launcher and real WM_DROPFILES input loaded the synthetic media/document, played, sought and paused without decoder/texture errors. Actual MCP stdio retained 45 tools and completed read/edit/export/FinishTask with original words, voices and inputs preserved. Private reports/captures are retained in data/reports. Linux/macOS execution is unvalidated, matching the product's prior platform status.

No transcription-quality improvement is implied by this interface migration. Phonon, Community-1 and NVIDIA inference logic, downloads and installed weights are unchanged.

CyUI license: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI/blob/main/LICENSE. The complete MIT text ships with the application, including when the upstream repository is private.

pages.title: Optional Community-1 speaker diarization
pages.html:
Optional Community-1 speaker diarization#

NVIDIA Nemotron 3 is a separate optional CPU/CUDA alternative: see NvidiaDiarization.md. This page describes Community-1.

Community-1 supplies global regular and exclusive speaker timelines. Phonon remains the transcription engine. Model: pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1, pinned revision 3533c8cf8e369892e6b79ff1bf80f7b0286a54ee, CC-BY-4.0. Source: https://huggingface.co/pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1.

Installation and credentials#

The Windows base archive contains no weights or diarization runtime. Installation downloads pinned, hashed wheels into a fresh runtime/components/diarization candidate, verifies imports in a fresh CPU process, then atomically activates it. Failed or cancelled candidates do not replace an earlier working component. Private Phonon dependencies are unchanged. Full package pins and official URLs are in diarization-runtime-lock.json; installed wheels retain their own license notices.

Open the model page, accept its conditions with your own account, then download through Installation. The Tool never accepts those conditions automatically. Its protected Windows read credential takes precedence over an existing Hugging Face login. The token is never a business parameter, command argument, saved generation field or model metadata entry. Community-1's telemetry is disabled for this Tool.

Local registration references the model directory in place, verifies the fixed Community-1 pipeline class and contained $model assets, and stores file hashes in the Tool registry. Custom Python classes and external asset references are rejected. Files are not moved.

Execution and outputs#

The optional CPU worker uses a separate dependency path with Pyannote 4.0.7, torch 2.8.0+cpu and torchaudio 2.8.0+cpu. It converts job-owned mono PCM16 audio into a disk-backed float waveform one minute at a time. Pyannote's own sliding analysis and bounded batch sizes analyze the complete recording with global speaker clustering; independent Phonon windows never restart speaker numbering. An explicit duration policy refuses audio longer than four hours at most. Native memory/time behavior on long files remains workload-dependent and has not been certified at that limit.

Original word text/timestamps remain immutable. Generation/reflow can split speech at speaker changes using temporary attributed word copies. Existing-document analysis keeps manual cue text/times by default. Manual speaker assignments persist unless replacement is requested. A duration mismatch, or a changed source hash after a prior analysis, is rejected. This does not prove that an unanalyzed old JSON document matches an arbitrary same-length media file; the user must select the matching recording.

JSON schemaVersion 1 gains optional speakers, diarization, speakerLabels, and per-cue speaker, speakerManual, speakerCandidates, speakerOverlapFraction. The fraction measures temporal overlap with an exclusive speaker region, not calibrated model confidence. Uncovered speech stays unassigned. A cue spanning multiple voices keeps reviewable candidates; explicit rebuild can split it using original words. Sound descriptions are never treated as speech.

SRT/VTT can display a plain [Name] prefix. Raw cue text stays separate. Visible names count towards reading-speed checks and bounded timing repair, which does not merge cues belonging to different speakers. Renaming does not change words or timing. Speaker labels are per-recording anonymous identities, not person recognition across files.

Public operations#

  • diarization_status: local readiness without importing the neural engine.
  • check_diarization_access: structured Accessible/AccessRequired; authenticated network permission.
  • install_diarization_runtime, install_diarization_model: explicit license review and network permission; candidate activation, private lock and retained diagnostics.
  • register_diarization_model: compatible local directory reference with hashes.
  • diarize_subtitles: original media plus document, count/bounds, threads, duration, batch sizes, labels and explicit rebuild/manual replacement flags.
  • rename_speakers: name map and label display preference; creates a new bundle.
  • edit_subtitles: optional speaker ID or null on each cue patch.

All media/document file fields participate in automatic private task import. Job workspaces and intermediates use JobContext.path; workers stop before reservations release and scratch files are removed. Export wanted bundles before FinishTask. The standalone uses retained sessions. All native business settings are exposed through generation configuration or Advanced operations.

Validation state#

Executed on Windows x64: the real optional runtime installer, wheel hashes, fresh CPU import, gated access refusal, speaker preservation/layout/validation tests, authenticated rename/edit/read/export/task cleanup, and actual GUI rename/manual assignment jobs in English/French. Original video preview regression checks remain in the suite.

After the user accepted the official access conditions, the pinned Community-1 weights downloaded successfully and passed the model catalog/hash checks. Real CPU inference attributed the existing single-voice sample to one person. A 44.55-second Windows SAPI recording with two alternating English/French voices was then transcribed with Phonon-2.5 and diarized with automatic speaker count (bounds 1–4): the model returned two speakers and correctly matched all four alternating turns. The combined run took 69.34 seconds with two CPU threads on this machine. This short synthetic recording is an integration check, not a benchmark of natural dialogue, overlapping speech or difficult audio.

A real MCP re-analysis of the same recording took 57.33 seconds, preserved original words and cue text/times, then completed renaming, SRT/VTT/JSON export and temporary-task cleanup. The Windows launcher rendered the installed runtime/model state. Private recordings, weights and reports are excluded from distribution. For Community-1, GPU and Linux/macOS are not integrated. Cross-recording identity, training and voiceprint exports are unavailable.

Caption boundary repair — 0.5.1#

Separate closing punctuation is grouped with its preceding word before layout, respecting the configured pause. Word/voice alignment may use a nearest region only within 250 ms when there is no direct overlap; long uncovered gaps stay unassigned. A weak mixed boundary (under 60% dominant word coverage) can retain the previous voice when that voice still overlaps at least 25% of the word. A nearby fallback without direct overlap can follow a well-covered next word in the same unfinished phrase. Fully covered short replies retain their own speaker.

These rules affect temporary layout copies, never original words or raw regular/exclusive model timelines. They prevent timestamp jitter and separately timed punctuation from fragmenting captions. They cannot repair an incorrect neural speaker clustering decision or recover missed/wrong transcription. Existing-document analysis still preserves manual cue text and timing unless rebuild is requested.

pages.title: Optional NVIDIA Nemotron 3 — 0.6.0
pages.html:
Optional NVIDIA Nemotron 3 — 0.6.0#

This component attributes voices; Phonon still supplies recognized text and original word timestamps. Community-1 remains available separately. NVIDIA uses the official native NeMo-Speech.cpp v0.2.0 runtime, not another Python ML environment.

Installation and licenses#

The base archive contains no NVIDIA runtime or model weights. Installation offers independent Windows x64 CPU and CUDA runtime downloads, native diagnostics, model download and compatible local GGUF reference. Review the Apache 2.0 runtime and OpenMDW 1.1 model terms and explicitly select the acceptance checkbox. Network operations require authenticated network permission and license_accepted: true; default false never accepts terms implicitly. No access token is required for this ungated model.

The official model is pinned to revision f667ed73aee57d40cc39428eb768b4fd87a0a29e, file Nemotron-3-Diarization.q8_0.gguf, 107,012,128 bytes, SHA256 08456d9e22cd9a323c0364d98375f3746d6e68507ebb705cd46438c534c7a3a1. This is Q8_0 quantization. Runtime archive hashes, sizes and URLs are in nemotron-catalog.json. CPU download is about 6 MB, CUDA about 102 MB. Each native archive carries its component notices; root LICENCES includes runtime, third-party and model terms with upstream links.

SDK InstallationStorage supplies the verified resumable download cache. Active installations remain private in runtime/components/nemotron and data/models/nemotron; sharing a download cache does not share the active installation. A fresh candidate is version/probe/hash checked before atomic activation. Failure or cancellation preserves the previous active candidate. Local registration verifies the exact official GGUF without moving it. No driver changes, global PATH edits, Phonon/Pyannote torch replacements or model relocation occur.

Options and processing#

Enable Identify different speakers and select NVIDIA Nemotron 3, then CPU or CUDA. The same fields exist in transcribe, diarize_subtitles, Advanced operations and versioned configuration JSON. Loading a configuration never starts a job. nemotron_status reports local presence without engine imports; nemotron_diagnostics checks the selected native runtime and actual hardware compatibility. A CUDA selection fails explicitly if unavailable rather than silently falling back to CPU.

The default chunked v3-offline quality preset uses stateful Sortformer caches across the recording. v3-streaming favors lower latency; custom exposes chunk, right/left context, FIFO, speaker-cache and update-period geometry in native 80 ms frames. Native activity options are onset, offset, onset/offset padding and minimum on/off durations. Zero padding/duration values are valid. Geometry overrides require the custom chunked preset; incompatible options are rejected before submission. Full attention uses --offline, is limited to 360 seconds, and cannot combine with a custom/streaming preset. The overall configured refusal limit is at most four hours; memory, time and accuracy at that bound are not certified.

The engine automatically detects up to eight anonymous voices. Community-1 speaker-count/batch fields must remain at their default sentinel values when NVIDIA is selected. CPU threads caps the one-shot worker's CPU affinity, inherited by the native child, rather than claiming a nonexistent native CLI thread flag. The actual device and CPU cap are recorded. SDK resources reserve CPU/RAM and estimated CUDA VRAM before execution. CUDA estimates are 2 GiB for named chunked presets and 6 GiB for full/custom; actual memory is workload-dependent.

Job-owned mono 16 kHz PCM16 and result scratch files use JobContext.path. ProcessWorker owns the native descendant, keeps reservations until shutdown, and removes scratch after stopping. No UI or neural imports enter the Core or Tool module import. Native logs remain available in selectable/copyable diagnostics. Task inputs import automatically; export wanted results before FinishTask. Desktop sessions retain their data.

Outputs and review#

Raw overlapping NVIDIA segments remain intact. A derived single-caption timeline chooses the previously active voice while it remains active, otherwise the earliest active region. This policy is recorded as previous-active-then-earliest; it is a Tool layout decision, not a native exclusive-speaker prediction. Cues retain raw overlap candidates. Uncovered speech remains unassigned and the desktop displays its count.

Original words/timestamps and existing caption text/times are preserved by attribution. Explicit rebuild recreates speech captions from original words; sound captions remain. Switching models creates new anonymous identities instead of inheriting the previous engine's names. Existing manual speaker assignments require explicit replacement before such a switch. Same-engine manual overrides retain the existing behavior. Names are display labels, not biometric recognition.

Operations: nemotron_status, nemotron_diagnostics, install_nemotron_runtime, install_nemotron_model, register_nemotron_model; common diarize_subtitles, rename_speakers, edit_subtitles, read_subtitles and export operations remain available.

Validation and limits#

Windows x64 CPU and CUDA on an RTX 3090 were executed on a 39.3-second natural recording, retaining the same Phonon words. NVIDIA returned seven alternating main-dialogue turns across two voices, improving this example's separation compared with Community-1. Some later speech remained unassigned. This is a qualitative comparison without a human reference annotation, not a diarization error-rate benchmark. Transcription errors are unchanged by this engine.

Authenticated controller analysis, including extraction/checks, took approximately 1.4 seconds on CUDA and 2.1 seconds on CPU for this short recording. These are speaker-analysis times, not complete subtitle-generation times or promises for other hardware/files. Full attention also completed. Real Windows EXE generation, configuration roundtrip, MCP re-analysis/rename/export/cleanup and native-child cancellation were verified. See Validation.md. Linux/macOS and multi-GPU execution remain unvalidated/unavailable in this adapter.

The official model is pinned to revision f667ed73aee57d40cc39428eb768b4fd87a0a29e , file Nemotron-3-Diarization.q8_0.gguf , 107,012,128 bytes, SHA256 08456d9e22cd9a323c0364d98375f3746d6e68507ebb705cd46438c534c7a3a1 . This is Q8_0 quantization. Runtime archive hashes, sizes and URLs are in nemotron-catalog.json . CPU download is about 6 MB, CUDA about 102 MB. Each native archive carries its component notices; root LICENCES includes runtime, third-party and model terms with upstream links. SDK InstallationStorage supplies the verified resumable download cache. Active installations remain private in runtime/components/nemotron and data/models/nemotron; sharing a download cache does not share the active installation. A fresh candidate is version/probe/hash checked before atomic activation. Failure or cancellation preserves the previous active candidate. Local registration verifies the exact official GGUF without moving it. No driver changes, global PATH edits, Phonon/Pyannote torch replacements or model relocation occur. Options and processing # Enable Identify different speakers and select NVIDIA Nemotron 3, then CPU or CUDA. The same fields exist in transcribe, diarize_subtitles, Advanced operations and versioned configuration JSON. Loading a configuration never starts a job. nemotron_status reports local presence without engine imports; nemotron_diagnostics checks the selected native runtime and actual hardware compatibility. A CUDA selection fails explicitly if unavailable rather than silently falling back to CPU. The default chunked v3-offline quality preset uses stateful Sortformer caches across the recording. v3-streaming favors lower latency; custom exposes chunk, right/left context, FIFO, speaker-cache and update-period geometry in native 80 ms frames. Native activity options are onset, offset, onset/offset padding and minimum on/off durations. Zero padding/duration values are valid. Geometry overrides require the custom chunked preset; incompatible options are rejected before submission. Full attention uses --offline , is limited to 360 seconds, and cannot combine with a custom/streaming preset. The overall configured refusal limit is at most four hours; memory, time and accuracy at that bound are not certified. The engine automatically detects up to eight anonymous voices. Community-1 speaker-count/batch fields must remain at their default sentinel values when NVIDIA is selected. CPU threads caps the one-shot worker's CPU affinity, inherited by the native child, rather than claiming a nonexistent native CLI thread flag. The actual device and CPU cap are recorded. SDK resources reserve CPU/RAM and estimated CUDA VRAM before execution. CUDA estimates are 2 GiB for named chunked presets and 6 GiB for full/custom; actual memory is workload-dependent. Job-owned mono 16 kHz PCM16 and result scratch files use JobContext.path. ProcessWorker owns the native descendant, keeps reservations until shutdown, and removes scratch after stopping. No UI or neural imports enter the Core or Tool module import. Native logs remain available in selectable/copyable diagnostics. Task inputs import automatically; export wanted results before FinishTask. Desktop sessions retain their data. Outputs and review # Raw overlapping NVIDIA segments remain intact. A derived single-caption timeline chooses the previously active voice while it remains active, otherwise the earliest active region. This policy is recorded as previous-active-then-earliest ; it is a Tool layout decision, not a native exclusive-speaker prediction. Cues retain raw overlap candidates. Uncovered speech remains unassigned and the desktop displays its count. Original words/timestamps and existing caption text/times are preserved by attribution. Explicit rebuild recreates speech captions from original words; sound captions remain. Switching models creates new anonymous identities instead of inheriting the previous engine's names. Existing manual speaker assignments require explicit replacement before such a switch. Same-engine manual overrides retain the existing behavior. Names are display labels, not biometric recognition. Operations: nemotron_status, nemotron_diagnostics, install_nemotron_runtime, install_nemotron_model, register_nemotron_model; common diarize_subtitles, rename_speakers, edit_subtitles, read_subtitles and export operations remain available. Validation and limits # Windows x64 CPU and CUDA on an RTX 3090 were executed on a 39.3-second natural recording, retaining the same Phonon words. NVIDIA returned seven alternating main-dialogue turns across two voices, improving this example's separation compared with Community-1. Some later speech remained unassigned. This is a qualitative comparison without a human reference annotation, not a diarization error-rate benchmark. Transcription errors are unchanged by this engine. Authenticated controller analysis, including extraction/checks, took approximately 1.4 seconds on CUDA and 2.1 seconds on CPU for this short recording. These are speaker-analysis times, not complete subtitle-generation times or promises for other hardware/files. Full attention also completed. Real Windows EXE generation, configuration roundtrip, MCP re-analysis/rename/export/cleanup and native-child cancellation were verified. See Validation.md. Linux/macOS and multi-GPU execution remain unvalidated/unavailable in this adapter.

pages.title: App-only release format
pages.html:
App-only release format#

Configure an owner/repository in Updates. Publish latest-release assets cytools-app.zip and cytools-app.zip.sha256 (a SHA256 hex string). ZIP contains app/ only, including CyTool.json and release.json. Manifest ID: cy.tools.subtitle. Fixed runtime ABI: py311-fermion0214-core0101-subtitle1. Platform: win32 or any. Maximum uncompressed contents: 256 MiB / 10,000 entries. Archive members must be confined regular files/directories, with no symlinks or traversal.

The source package is distinct: it also includes the native launchers and guide, and excludes data/, runtime/, weights and caches. App-only releases preserve the existing tested environment and cannot add dependencies. Build/test a new environment before changing ABI or redistributing a runtime. The activation lock and active-process checks defer replacement while jobs or another app instance are present. Failed activation restores the original app; the previous version remains selectable.

pages.title: Optional PyTorch runtime — 0.3.0
pages.html:
Optional PyTorch runtime — 0.3.0#

The Windows base ZIP includes CPython and the media/UI runtime. It excludes PyTorch, SymPy, NetworkX and mpmath. Preview, subtitle editing and timing repair work without those packages.

Desktop#

Open Installation. Review the PyTorch license, enable its checkbox and click Download / repair PyTorch. Watch the job status and Application log. Cancel requests stop the installer worker and descendants before resources are released. After a successful CPU import check the component becomes active; no application restart is needed for subsequent generation workers. Then install or register the desired Phonon model.

MCP / CLI#

  • runtime_status {} returns Installed/Missing, readiness, exact expected/detected package versions, source/license links and verification information.
  • install_runtime {"license_accepted":true,"repair":false} downloads pinned CPU packages when missing. The transport identity must have network permission. Use repair:true to build a new candidate even when the current component is installed.
  • Poll the job through its terminal state. A cancellation request is not confirmation that the worker has stopped. A failed download leaves the old activation record intact; retry creates another candidate and can use the normal pip download cache.

The installer only targets private directories under runtime/components/pytorch. It never replaces Python, edits a system installation, moves existing models, changes drivers or swaps CUDA libraries. Package names, versions and the HTTPS package index are fixed by the Tool; no arbitrary package names or commands are accepted.

Candidate directories and cached downloads are persistent installation state, not temporary AI task outputs. FinishTask does not uninstall a completed component. Base release packaging excludes these directories, so building a ZIP after local installation still does not bundle PyTorch.

The guided installer currently supports Windows CPython 3.11 CPU. Other platforms remain unvalidated. Model weights retain their own licenses and installation flow. Source development environments may install the full requirements.txt directly.

pages.title: Task files — SDK 0.9.0
pages.html:
SDK reference retained from the application sources. Its SDK version may differ from this application; the current operation reference is generated from CyTool.json.

Task files — SDK 0.9.0#

SDK sessions are temporary by default. A task can contain several jobs; completion of one producer must not delete results needed by consumers. Models, application code, shared installation caches and the original source files are never task artifacts.

Tool implementation (mandatory)#

Configure the accepted input root once in create_runtime, before starting:

python
runtime.configure_inputs(DATA / 'inputs', fields={    'image_to_mesh': ['image_file'],    'synthesize': ['references.*.audio'],})

Use the same root as the existing input resolver (including any configured environment variable). Declare every input-file field, including nested array fields. These fields accept absolute external paths; the SDK copies the source into a unique task-owned subdirectory of the accepted input root before calling the handler. Existing relative paths are also copied. A model path, LoRA, export destination or executable is NOT an input artifact: do not declare these in fields. Keep file format/size validation in the handler. The shared import bundle limit defaults to 8 GiB, configurable by the Tool. All generated files, intermediate files and worker diagnostics MUST use JobContext.path. Never write generated media into a global directory. Explicit user saves (profiles, model registration, installation) remain persistent operations.

AI / MCP use#

  • Call operations with an absolute input path directly; no shell copy is required.
  • Or call cy_import_file({"source":"D:/project/image.png"}). The Tool process copies it and returns path (absolute), relativePath, SHA256 and size. Supply path to the operation. OBJ/MTL/textures and GLTF/BIN references are copied automatically. Additional files can be passed as companions, relative paths from the source directory; directory structure is preserved. Import the bundle before submitting it. This never downloads a model.
  • Poll cy_get_job; read/consume the results while the task remains open.
  • To preserve a result, use cy_export_job({"jobId":"...","destination":"D:/project/results"}). This copies the job bundle, including supporting files, into a unique destination directory outside the runtime; returned output paths point to the exported copy.
  • Call cy_finish_task({}) after all consumers finish. It removes imported copies AND whole job workspaces: generated results, intermediates and logs. It never removes the original files or the explicit exported bundle. An active worker returns Busy; cancelRunning:true requests cancellation and defers deletion until workers stop.
  • Disconnect also finishes all connection-owned tasks. A forgotten idle task expires after 3600 seconds by default. cy_keep_task_alive renews it; active workers are never removed by expiration. cy_begin_task accepts retentionSeconds (1..86400). Its returned sessionId can be passed to operation envelopes and task controls for concurrent task graphs. Finish each Tool's task only after downstream consumers have imported or consumed its output. Paths between machines require a transfer transport; a local path refers to the Tool's host.

SDK equivalents: CreateSession, ImportFile, SubmitJob, ExportJob, FinishTask, KeepTaskAlive; same authenticated ownership in JSONL and HTTP. Native Python:

python
with runtime.task(actor) as session_id:    job = runtime.submit(actor, session_id, 'image_to_mesh', {'image_file': source})    result = runtime.wait(actor, job['jobId'], timeout=300)    saved = runtime.export_job(actor, job['jobId'], destination)

The context manager closes on exceptions as well. Normal runtime shutdown cleans remaining temporary tasks. On restart, recorded temporary tasks are recovered for cleanup; recorded live worker processes block deletion. A redirected workspace or a locked file produces cleanupError and retries, never an unsafe recursive deletion. Do not claim that an OS-denied source can be read: the MCP must return a useful error.

Standalone and compatibility#

Interactive UI sessions MUST explicitly use temporary=False; their generated results remain available after closing the UI. Imported working copies still disappear on session/runtime close. CLI invoke and saved-configuration replay remain persistent for backwards compatibility. AI automation should use task sessions via SDK/MCP. Pre-0.9 sessions have no temporary flag and are preserved; there is no destructive migration of old inputs/results. Small SQLite job/session history remains, with the parameters and output payload removed for purged jobs (artifactsDeleted:true). Model weights and secrets must not be put into a job workspace or export bundle.

Verification required before delivery#

Test external image/audio/video/mesh inputs without manually placing them under the Tool; assert the real resolver accepts the staged path. Test bundles, failed/cancelled jobs, disconnect, expiration, exports, client isolation and a worker still running. Verify every configured file field, not only one selected Tool. A transport test is not proof of a new full AI inference run; report the distinction explicitly.

pages.title: Tool delivery checklist
pages.html:
SDK reference retained from the application sources. Its SDK version may differ from this application; the current operation reference is generated from CyTool.json.

Tool delivery checklist#

Follow StandaloneDelivery, FullOperationAccess and TaskFiles before delivering a Tool.

  • Validate the manifest and execute its automated tests.
  • Launch the standalone from outside its installation folder; verify English/French, configuration persistence, copyable logs and every exposed business operation.
  • Exercise CLI and real MCP calls, including external inputs, result export, cancellation and task cleanup after workers stop.
  • Validate real model inference separately from synthetic transport tests.
  • Record the executed platform, model revision, output format and resource measurements.
  • Keep machine-specific reports under the Tool's data/reports directory.
  • State untested platforms and operations explicitly. A scaffold alone is not a delivery.

pages.title: Unreal integration
pages.html:
Unreal integration#

CyUEMCPSDK adapts CyToolsCore contracts to Unreal plugins. Follow its Docs/Integration.md and Docs/UpdateExistingPlugin.md. For an existing plugin, embed and adapt the C++ sources into its existing modules; the separate reference plugins are development examples, not mandatory dependencies. The Python companion uses CyToolsCore without copying its runtime or schemas.

pages.title: Validation — 2026-10-24, Windows x64
pages.html:
Validation — 2026-10-24, Windows x64#

Actual Python 3.11 private runtime with CyToolsCore 0.10.1 MIT wheel, Fermion 0.2.14, imgui-bundle 1.93.0, PyAV 18.1.0, sounddevice 0.5.6 and imageio-ffmpeg 0.6.0.

Executed evidence in ../../data/reports/:

  • real-inference.json: Phonon-2 English, synthesized local speech, 5-second core windows, 2-second overlap, voice filter, 32-character layout and 2 CPU threads. All reference words recovered in this sample; no cue warnings.
  • real-inference-fr.json: Phonon-2.5 French speech, 8-second windows, explicit Bonjour vocabulary and strength 1.5. French accents preserved in UTF-8 subtitles.
  • delivery-integration.json: 640x360 video, physical audio output, pause/seek; actual MCP transcription and metadata/excerpt, read/edit/add sound/reflow/export, task cleanup; real inference cancellation with worker termination before reservations release.
  • preview.png and options EN/FR captures: actual Dear ImGui rendering with video subtitle overlay, persistent preference controls and configuration controls.
  • test_tool.py: cue timing/layout/export, malformed documents, private imports/client isolation, export/FinishTask, invalid schemas/media, missing model, worker diagnostics, cancellation, independent operations, generation configuration round trip, confined update archive/activation/rollback and data preservation.
  • SDK regression suite: 135 passed. SDK distribution build succeeded; wheel contains portable schemas and templates.

The transcript checks cover short synthetic samples, not a large quality benchmark or difficult audio. Window memory is bounded by construction; 24-hour recordings have not been stress-tested. Preview clock behavior was exercised on this machine, not certified across all audio drivers/codecs. Linux/macOS, CUDA and MLX have not been validated. The English-specific Phonon-2.5-en variant is offered but has no separate real inference result. No public application GitHub repository is configured; updater verification used local archive fixtures rather than a live public release. The source-installation venv depends on system Python. Version 0.2.2 also supplies the separately validated Windows portable runtime described below.

Timing repair 0.2.0#

Actual private SDK remains MIT 0.10.1. Timing uses the already-installed SciPy 1.17.1, now explicitly pinned as a direct dependency.

The repair operation was exercised on a long-form French recording through a real MCP stdio client, followed by export and FinishTask. Original word timestamps and normalized speech text are identical before/after. Caption count 629 -> 561, reading-speed warnings 102 -> 11, overlaps 2 -> 0. Remaining fast dialogue stays flagged within the default synchronization limits; a structural test does not establish audio or linguistic accuracy. Source recordings, generated subtitles and local reports are not distributed.

Tests cover hard early/late/end bounds, rounded output/media end, raw-word/sound/manual-text preservation, repeated repairs without drift, malformed timing policy, legacy configuration loading, and real private-input/export/cleanup. SDK regression suite: 135 passed.

Windows portable release 0.2.2#

A new application-local CPython 3.11.9 x64 embeddable runtime was built from the official python.org archive with a pinned SHA256. Dependencies were installed into a clean directory using windows-constraints.txt; the development venv was not copied. Native Windows launcher rebuilt with Visual Studio 2022. The Tool and its application sources use AGPL-3.0-only; the SDK and third-party components retain their original licenses.

The complete directory was moved to a different path containing spaces and an accented character. Python runs in isolated mode; Torch, NumPy, SciPy, PyAV, MCP, sounddevice, ImGui and Windows integration imported from that moved runtime. CLI describe returned the application manifest. The actual .exe was launched from another working directory: the English Options render closed after 16 frames and the GUI timing-repair operation completed through a worker.

A real MCP stdio session using the relocated interpreter inspected a 640x360 video and transcribed its audio into 27 words and 5 cues in approximately 11.2 seconds on this test machine. The test edited a cue, exported the result, finished the temporary task and verified that only the exported result remained. Preview opened physical audio output, decoded video pixels, played and sought successfully. Installed local models were referenced for this test; weights and test media are not included in the release.

The 21 Tool tests passed after switching the worker to module-based Phonon invocation. These checks cover this Windows machine; they do not establish portability across every Windows version, codec or audio device. The repository is private at this delivery: releases can be downloaded through an authenticated browser, while the in-app updater currently expects public release URLs. Update activation/rollback remain validated with local fixtures rather than a private authenticated download.

Optional PyTorch download — 0.3.0#

The Windows base runtime was rebuilt without Torch, SymPy, NetworkX and mpmath. A relocated clean installation returned Missing and could not resolve the torch module. The actual Windows .exe rendered the Installation tab in English and French without Torch, showing the license review and download controls.

A real authenticated MCP session checked runtime_status, verified refusal without explicit license review, started install_runtime and cancelled after observing the pip child process. The job reached Cancelled only after that child stopped; no active component pointer was created. A subsequent real PyPI installation downloaded PyTorch 2.14.1 and its fixed private math dependencies, passed a separate CPU import check and activated the component in about 62.7 seconds on this machine. Existing model files were referenced in place. Video transcription then produced 27 words and 5 cues, followed by export and temporary-task cleanup.

The automated suite now has 24 passing tests. New coverage checks missing runtime status, path confinement, authenticated network and license requirements, and preservation of the previous active installation when candidate verification fails. Downloaded component directories and caches are excluded from base packaging even after successful local tests. Guided component installation is Windows/CPython 3.11 CPU only; Linux/macOS remain unvalidated.

CyUI desktop — 0.4.0 (2026-10-25)#

The Tool integrates the author-provided CyUI Python port, with its MIT notice and source fingerprints. The local backup commit before integration is recorded in Git. The only vendor adjustments adapt draw flags and text pointer arguments to imgui-bundle 1.93.0; the upstream framework directory is unchanged.

Windows GUI checks exercised all five themes and compact/comfortable density, English/French, a 1024×768 window, real video playback with subtitle overlay, cue search layout, a timing repair through the existing runtime, Options configuration save/load, selectable logs and native clipboard round trip, and complete advanced-operation access. The 24 existing Tool/timing tests passed using the delivered CPython 3.11.9 and private development test tools. No inference algorithm or operation contract changed. Legacy theme preferences and language/text-size persistence were checked.

A fresh portable product without PyTorch or model weights launched through its actual EXE from another working directory. Its workspace rendered the guided missing-PyTorch state and remained usable. The private installed product retains its separately downloaded runtime and models. Linux/macOS and higher-DPI hardware were not exercised; DPI scaling uses the platform factor supplied by HelloImGui.

Video preview and native file drop — 0.4.1 (2026-10-25)#

A real 1676×992 screen capture reproduced the preview failure: PyAV exposed RGB rows with padding, while the image binding requires packed C-contiguous memory. Initial probe and subsequent decode/seek now use the same bounded RGB conversion; the UI holds one frame reference through its draw and reports rendering errors without closing the application. The capture was exercised through playback, seek and pause after the fix.

External file drops are connected to the existing bundled GLFW window, with callback lifetime and cleanup before window destruction. The callback queues UTF-8 paths for processing on a normal UI frame, through the same opener as the file picker. Windows tests verified the Explorer acceptance style and delivered actual WM_DROPFILES events to that window: video, an accented audio path, video with subtitle JSON, and a refused text file. Tests did not synthesize a mouse drag gesture. Files remain at their original locations, and dropping does not submit generation.

The suite passed 30 tests, including four padded capture widths, first-frame and seek-frame packing, and invalid video error handling. No model or PyTorch dependency was added. Windows x64 was exercised; native drop integration on Linux/macOS remains unvalidated.

Optional speaker diarization — 0.5.0 (2026-10-25)#

The isolated Windows CPU runtime installed successfully from 95 pinned, hashed wheels. A fresh process imported Pyannote 4.0.7 with torch/torchaudio 2.8.0+cpu. The separate Phonon torch 2.14.1+cpu installation was preserved; a subsequent real Phonon transcription produced 26 words and 5 cues.

The product suite passes 48 tests. Speaker coverage includes preservation of words/manual text/times/sounds, voice-change layout, visible-name reading speed, manual attribution, reduced-speaker reanalysis, local reference hashes and preflight, malformed metadata, missing access, authenticated license/permission checks, failed candidate activation and job scratch cleanup. The operation test uses a declared timeline worker fixture; it does not establish neural recognition accuracy.

Actual Windows GUI jobs renamed people and changed a cue's speaker in English and French. A real MCP stdio session discovered the new operations, renamed a speaker, exported subtitles and finished its temporary task, verifying cleanup while preserving the exported files and original document. Installation and Options were rendered with the optional runtime present and model absent.

After explicit acceptance of the official conditions, Community-1 downloaded at the pinned revision and passed its catalog/hash checks. Actual CPU inference succeeded on the original one-voice recording. Combined Phonon-2.5 transcription plus Community-1 analysis of a 44.55-second synthetic English/French conversation took 69.34 seconds with two threads. Automatic count (1–4) found two speakers and correctly associated each of the four alternating turns with its voice. A real MCP re-analysis took 57.33 seconds and preserved words, caption text and times; renaming, export and FinishTask cleanup also passed. The installed model/runtime state rendered through the actual Windows launcher.

These are short synthetic integration samples, not a quality benchmark for natural dialogue, simultaneous speakers or background noise. They do not establish a general processing-speed guarantee. See Diarization for the execution contract and limits. No gated weights or optional runtime are included in the base release.

A clean relocated 0.5.0 base package launched through its actual Windows EXE from a different working directory without torch, the optional diarization runtime or model weights. Its editor completed real rename/manual-assignment jobs, and its French Installation page rendered both missing-component states and guided installation controls.

Caption boundary repair — 0.5.1#

A user recording of 39.3 seconds exposed punctuation-only captions and spurious one-word splits when word timestamps and voice regions differed by a few frames. The same media and generation parameters were run again with Phonon-2.5 and Community-1 after the correction. The output changed from 15 to 8 captions, removed the isolated exclamation/question marks, and preserved the original recognized words and their timestamps exactly. The original recording/results remain unchanged.

The suite passes 54 tests, including punctuation at sentence ends, layout duration/pause limits, bounded near-region attribution, unchanged raw timelines, ambiguous word boundaries and clearly covered short speaker replies. This validates a reproduced segmentation fix; it does not establish correct transcription or neural speaker identities throughout this natural recording.

The actual Windows GUI loaded this capture and the corrected JSON through native file-drop events, decoded packed frames, played, sought and paused without a preview error.

Optional NVIDIA voice analysis — 0.6.0#

The pinned CPU/CUDA NeMo-Speech.cpp v0.2.0 runtime and official Q8_0 model were installed through authenticated Tool operations after explicit human license acceptance. Native diagnostics confirmed CUDA compatibility on an RTX 3090. Phonon/Pyannote dependencies and existing models were unchanged.

On the same 39.3-second natural recording and Phonon-2.5 word evidence, authenticated controller analysis took 1.437 s in CUDA chunked mode and 2.109 s on CPU. CUDA full attention took 1.438 s. These include extraction and verification and exclude transcription; they are not general speed guarantees. CPU/CUDA chunked output matched, with seven alternating main-dialogue turns across two anonymous voices. This separated the principal exchange better than Community-1 in this example, while later speech remained unassigned. No annotated reference or formal accuracy score exists for this sample.

The actual Windows launcher completed Phonon-2.5 plus NVIDIA CUDA generation with nine phrase captions and no timing warnings. Original transcription mistakes remain possible. The selected device and NVIDIA settings survived configuration save/load. Real MCP stdio discovered 45 operations, performed CUDA attribution with a nondefault CPU cap, preserved original words/text/times, renamed voices and exported SRT/VTT/JSON. FinishTask removed imported/workspace copies after export and retained original inputs.

The 70-test suite passed, including overlapping voice candidates, invalid native results, incompatible parameter rejection, local hashes, explicit-license/authenticated-network checks, failed candidate preservation, CPU/CUDA resource estimates, cross-model manual-identity protection and real child affinity inheritance. A separate cancellation test observed the running native process, confirmed reservations while it was active, then verified descendant shutdown before resource release and task cleanup. Private media, transcripts, screenshots and installed optional components are excluded from release archives.

The native Windows file-drop path loaded the NVIDIA document with its matching media, played, sought into a spoken caption and paused with packed video frames and no preview error. NVIDIA settings/installation pages rendered in English/French, across all five themes and both densities; the custom geometry/segmentation panel was inspected. A real custom-preset run and a nondefault-threshold run with zero padding completed; neither recovered the two remaining unassigned captions in this sample.

Modular CyUI interface — 0.7.0#

86 tests pass in the private product runtime. Added coverage executes real ImGui move/trim gestures and commit/cancel/revision phases, common Inspector cancellation, command keyboard activation, stable EN/FR IDs, selected snapshot hash/import verification, history branching/budgets and atomic domain patches. All eight application views rendered through the Windows EXE in English/French across five themes and both densities. A synthetic padded-width video rendered through the GPU texture surface; a real edit job plus Undo/Redo preserved original word evidence. Headless style DPI checks cover 100–200%; physical monitor switching and Linux/macOS execution remain unvalidated. Detailed scope: CyUIMigration.md.

The launcher was rebuilt with MSVC x64. Real native file-drop testing opened both synthetic files, rendered packed video frames, played, sought and paused without errors. Actual MCP stdio retained 45 tools and completed document read/edit, SRT/VTT/JSON export and task cleanup with original words/voice records unchanged.

The 70-test suite passed, including overlapping voice candidates, invalid native results, incompatible parameter rejection, local hashes, explicit-license/authenticated-network checks, failed candidate preservation, CPU/CUDA resource estimates, cross-model manual-identity protection and real child affinity inheritance. A separate cancellation test observed the running native process, confirmed reservations while it was active, then verified descendant shutdown before resource release and task cleanup. Private media, transcripts, screenshots and installed optional components are excluded from release archives. The native Windows file-drop path loaded the NVIDIA document with its matching media, played, sought into a spoken caption and paused with packed video frames and no preview error. NVIDIA settings/installation pages rendered in English/French, across all five themes and both densities; the custom geometry/segmentation panel was inspected. A real custom-preset run and a nondefault-threshold run with zero padding completed; neither recovered the two remaining unassigned captions in this sample. Modular CyUI interface — 0.7.0 # 86 tests pass in the private product runtime. Added coverage executes real ImGui move/trim gestures and commit/cancel/revision phases, common Inspector cancellation, command keyboard activation, stable EN/FR IDs, selected snapshot hash/import verification, history branching/budgets and atomic domain patches. All eight application views rendered through the Windows EXE in English/French across five themes and both densities. A synthetic padded-width video rendered through the GPU texture surface; a real edit job plus Undo/Redo preserved original word evidence. Headless style DPI checks cover 100–200%; physical monitor switching and Linux/macOS execution remain unvalidated. Detailed scope: CyUIMigration.md . The launcher was rebuilt with MSVC x64. Real native file-drop testing opened both synthetic files, rendered packed video frames, played, sought and paused without errors. Actual MCP stdio retained 45 tools and completed document read/edit, SRT/VTT/JSON export and task cleanup with original words/voice records unchanged.

pages.title: Publishing the CyDoc reader
pages.html:
Publishing the CyDoc reader#

The web manual and the embedded manual are the same complete CyDoc HTML export. Markdown files remain editable sources; GitHub Pages serves the generated reader, including its navigation, full-text search, locales, styles, scripts and local media.

Regenerate and stage#

From the repository root, with Node.js 22+ and Python 3.11+:

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --install --checkpython app/tests/test_documentation.pypython app/tests/test_pages.pypython app/documentation/publish.py

The locked, vendored CyDoc package provides the generator. CI needs no access to the upstream private repository and installs no model or application engine. The publisher validates app/help and copies it byte-for-byte into _site, adding only .nojekyll and a staging marker. It never publishes application data/, runtime/, weights, credentials, conversations or generated user outputs. Do not hand-edit _site or app/help; edit the sources in sources.json instead. Source text hashes and indexed source copies use UTF-8 with LF newlines, and licence ordering is case-independent, so Windows and Linux produce the same reader. The original source documents are preserved.

Automatic deployment#

.github/workflows/documentation.yml rebuilds on pushes to main and can also be started manually from Actions. Only _site is uploaded to the github-pages artifact and deployed by the official Pages action. Set repository Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source to GitHub Actions.

The root English README links to #/en/overview, and the French README to #/fr/overview; the reader's language selector remains available on both. Page and section links use hash routes so they work beneath a project Pages URL and from an offline file:// URL without server rewrites.

Embedded help#

The full app/help remains in the application distribution. F1 and Options keep opening its local file URL. Publishing introduces no network dependency into embedded help and does not replace it with a web link.

Pages availability for this repository#

This repository is private and its current GitHub plan does not support Pages. The workflow builds the export, but deployment is disabled until Pages is available. No public documentation link is advertised before deployment. After Pages becomes available, select GitHub Actions in Settings → Pages, set the repository Actions variable DOCS_PAGES_ENABLED to true, and run the Documentation workflow. This does not require changing repository visibility.

pages.title: Local documentation (CyDoc)
pages.html:
Local documentation (CyDoc)#

The editable Markdown listed in sources.json remains the source of truth. build.py imports it into CyDoc with stable page IDs, local media, full operation schemas and a lexical index of the shipped app/tool.py. Original French guides are retained; absent translations are explicit and tracked. Do not hand-edit app/help.

From the application root (Node.js >=22 and npm are build requirements only):

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --installpython app/documentation/build.py --checkpython app/help_docs.py --page overview --locale en

--install installs the locked generator under runtime/documentation-build, outside the shipped application. Subsequent builds need no installation. An already built CyDoc checkout/package may be selected with --cydoc-root PATH.

The complete generated app/help/ is shipped with application/update archives. Open app/help/index.html through a file URL. F1 opens contextual help; Options provides manual and workspace buttons. No HTTP server, CDN, network request or Node.js is needed for reading. External reference links remain optional external navigation.

CyDoc is pinned in cydoc-source.json and distributed under MIT; its full notice is in this directory, app/help and root LICENCES. Preserve generated third-party notices. MeshStudio alone includes an original procedural GLB with the mesh module and Three.js. Other modules are selected from actual imported media. Unused module scripts are absent. No interactive graph, GIF decoder or video player is added merely because an application can produce that format.

Review app/help/migration-report.json for old/missing links and translation-report.json for missing/stale translations. SDK reference pages are labelled separately from actual application capabilities. Linux/macOS launchers remain unverified unless a validation report records an execution on those platforms.

Web documentation#

Public deployment is pending GitHub Pages availability for this private repository. See Publishing the reader for the GitHub Actions workflow and local staging commands. Embedded help continues to work offline.

pages.title: CyDoc migration validation
pages.html:
CyDoc migration validation#

Scope#

Existing user/developer guides, local illustrations, shipped operation schemas and the public Python entry-point source were migrated. The original Markdown is retained as editable source and for GitHub links. App/help is generated and includes all reader resources. Node.js is required only for regeneration; the reader uses local classic scripts and file URLs.

Checks executed on Windows#

  • Pinned CyDoc 0.1.0 built from revision 774f2a7eabf7dd181a98ffc5add115b580b67f42.
  • App-local npm lockfile installation and full CyDoc build/check.
  • Python routing tests: English/French, legacy paths, Unicode, spaces/hash characters, media links, unknown page fallback, browser failure, active operation and common anchors.
  • Native ImGui test-engine clicks on both help buttons and F1, using the product interpreter. The browser call was intercepted to assert its file URL without launching tabs.
  • The full standalone Options window was opened and closed in an isolated application copy.
  • Generated reader tested in a DOM fixture with network calls forbidden: rendering, operation links/anchors, language switch and in-window image expansion/Escape when used.
  • The pinned CyDoc core, interactions and packed-asset suites passed (25 tests), including keyboard/pointer controls and reading-position restoration.
  • Distribution selections are checked for the entire help tree and notices.

Limits#

The automation browser blocks file URLs. A real browser visual check of file-origin storage, layout, codecs and WebGL remains necessary; DOM fixtures do not prove it. Linux and macOS were not executed. Touch-device behavior is covered by library interaction fixtures, not a physical touch-device run. Existing missing translations remain visible in translation-report.json. No model inference was needed or rerun for this migration. The migration report records old missing references; SDK reference documents may describe older SDK releases and are explicitly labelled separately from current operation contracts.

Regenerate and verify#

From the application root:

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --installpython app/documentation/build.py --checkpython app/tests/test_documentation.pypython app/help_docs.py --page overview --locale en --print-url

Existing release builders regenerate/validate the manual before packaging. When a builder uses git archive, commit the generated reader together with its source changes first. Keep the complete app/help directory and LICENCES/CyDoc-MIT.txt in the delivered product.
