pages.title: CyTools_Subtitle 0.7.0
pages.html:
CyTools_Subtitle 0.7.0#

Local Phonon subtitles, word timing, native audio/video preview, cue editor and MCP API. Built with the actual CyToolsCore 0.10.1 MIT wheel, without copying its runtime sources. No media, UI or ML imports enter the Core.

Desktop#

Version 0.5.1 keeps separately timestamped punctuation with its words and handles small ASR/voice-boundary offsets when laying out captions. Ambiguous word-boundary changes use nearby phrase context; original word timestamps and raw model timelines are retained. This improves caption segmentation and does not guarantee correct speaker clustering or transcription.

Version 0.4.1 fixes preview of videos with padded RGB rows, including arbitrary capture widths. Drop an audio/video file anywhere on the main window to load its preview; a subtitle JSON document can also be dropped. Invalid files show an error without closing the application.

The CyUI interface provides a sidebar workspace, resizable preview/inspector columns, caption search and a separate cue editor. Options offers five semantic themes, compact/comfortable density and persistent text size; legacy dark/light/classic preferences migrate automatically. English is the default; French remains selectable. Shortcuts: Ctrl+O media, Ctrl+Shift+O subtitle JSON, Ctrl+R reload preview, Space play/pause, Left arrow back two seconds and Ctrl+S save a new subtitle bundle. Shortcuts do not intercept text entry.

The Windows portable release includes Python and media/UI dependencies; PyTorch is downloaded separately from Installation: extract the complete archive, then launch ../CyTools_Subtitle.exe. Source checkouts require install.ps1 first. English is the default; French is selectable in Options. Select an audio/video source and Generate subtitles. The player streams decoding off the UI thread, overlays active captions and supports pause/seek. Source and preview pixel dimensions are displayed. The editor changes individual cue text/start/end, shifts the track, adds sound captions and exports SRT/VTT/JSON. Reflow explicitly rebuilds speech from original word timings, replacing manual speech edits while preserving sound captions.

Phonon-2 and Phonon-2.5 English: English only. Phonon-2.5: multilingual, including French. Phonon does not translate or classify background sounds. Speaker attribution is available through optional Community-1 (CPU) or NVIDIA Nemotron 3 (CPU/CUDA) components. Phonon transcription remains CPU-only; NVIDIA device selection applies to voice analysis. LoRA is unsupported. Voice filtering is highpass/lowpass plus FFT denoise, not neural vocal separation.

The model receives sequential bounded WAV windows, with overlap and word-midpoint ownership at boundaries. A window is deleted/reused rather than accumulating complete recording tensors. Transcription errors and boundary omissions/repetitions remain possible: review the result. Decoder timing uses native frame resolution; no timing precision or transcript completeness guarantee. Truncated inference fails explicitly and requests shorter windows.

Operations#

  • transcribe: media, model/local directory, CPU threads, audio track, windows/overlap, filter, hotwords/strength and cue layout.
  • inspect_media: source stream metadata, dimensions and optional bounded WAV excerpt/waveform.
  • read_subtitles: paginated original words and current cues in a time range.
  • edit_subtitles: stable-ID text/timing patches, delete/add cues, sound descriptions and global offset. Writes a new bundle.
  • reflow_subtitles: rebuild speech cues from the original word timing evidence.
  • runtime_status / install_runtime: inspect or download/repair the optional pinned CPU PyTorch component, with explicit license review and authenticated network permission.
  • model_status / install_model / register_local_model: verify, download/repair and reference compatible local models.
  • installation_storage_status: SDK cache and Toolkit diagnostics.

All declared parameters and invocation envelopes are accessible in Advanced operations, with validation, estimation, priorities and deadlines. The manifest is the common contract for standalone/CLI/MCP/HTTP. Estimates are conservative envelopes, not measured upper-bound guarantees.

CLI and MCP#

From the Tool root on Windows:

powershell
.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py describe.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py describe-operation transcribe.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py --data-dir .\data\cli invoke transcribe --params-file .\app\params.json --timeout 3600.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py --data-dir .\data\mcp mcp

Replace the example media path in params.json. MCP configuration example: mcp-config.example.json. Run the private Python with app/make_mcp_config.py to print the absolute paths for your installation. Operation calls have a parameters envelope, for example op_transcribe with {"parameters":{"media":"D:/clips/example.mp4","model":"phonon-2.5"}}. Poll cy_get_job until Completed; errors/cancellation are terminal outcomes requiring review. Inspect the operation output schema before chaining outputs.

AI workflow: op_inspect_media -> op_transcribe -> op_read_subtitles -> op_edit_subtitles -> cy_export_job -> cy_finish_task. Inspect audio excerpts with an audio-capable model or a classifier before adding sound descriptions. A cue with kind=sound is reviewer-supplied, not a Phonon detection. Times use seconds from the media start. JSON retains original words, chunks, source dimensions, settings and reading-speed/overlap warnings.

Absolute local paths are automatically privately imported, including spaces/Unicode. No manual input copies. Original files stay intact. MCP tasks are temporary: FinishTask/disconnect removes task imports and workspaces after real workers stop. Export wanted results first. Desktop and CLI invoke sessions explicitly retain outputs. Independent MCP processes have separate queues; use authenticated shared HTTP/bridge when sharing one scheduler. Clients cannot read another client's private artifacts. Paths refer to the Tool host.

Install operations require the authenticated network permission and explicit public model license review. Provision a credential using create-client --name installer --permission network, then pass the token through the local CYTOOLS_TOKEN environment or authenticated transport. No tokens in parameters, recipes or Git.

Installation / updates#

The local runtime uses the real wheel in app/packages. install.ps1 creates a private venv at its final path using Python 3.11, then installs the pinned Windows base requirements without PyTorch. Install PyTorch through Installation before inference. The full requirements.txt remains available for development environments. install.sh is provided for Linux but unvalidated. Local venvs are not portable; model weights and environments are excluded from source releases.

Model catalog pins are copied from fermion-research==0.2.14 into model-catalog.json. The upstream downloader verifies archive hashes and supports retries; the Tool additionally hashes the local container against packed_manifest.json. Repair preserves damaged managed weights in a neighbouring .invalid-* directory. References require config.json, packed_manifest.json and matching model.fermion for the Phonon-2 family. No LoRA. Configurations contain only references, never weights/secrets. Changing shared cache settings never moves models, Python, PyTorch libraries or the system driver.

Updates requires a configured owner/repository. Expected latest-release assets: cytools-app.zip and cytools-app.zip.sha256. Only confined app/ files are accepted; Tool ID, runtime ABI, platform, SHA256, size/count limits and Python syntax are checked. Dependencies remain fixed; new dependencies require a separately tested runtime. Activation at restart preserves a previous app for rollback, with data/ and runtime/ untouched. Co-published checksums are not independent signatures. No public application repository is configured; update tests use local fixtures.

Verification and licenses#

Private Python: -m pytest app/test_tool.py -q. app/validate_delivery.py runs actual video transcription through MCP, corrections/reflow/export/FinishTask, native audio/video playback and seek, and real cancellation. It requires local validation samples, installed models and an audio device. Evidence: data/reports/. Details: Docs/CapabilityCoverage.md and Docs/Validation.md.

Copyright (c) 2026 Cyberalien. CyTools_Subtitle is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 only (AGPL-3.0-only); see LICENSE for the complete terms. The CyToolsCore SDK remains MIT.

Windows x64 validated locally. Linux/macOS Unknown. Component declarations and full installed notices: licenses.json, LICENCES/, LICENSE and LICENSE-CyToolsCore.txt. Model weights keep CC-BY-4.0; the Phonon runtime keeps Apache-2.0; FFmpeg builds retain their GPL/LGPL obligations.

Timing corrections in 0.2.0#

Generation and reflow now enable auto_timing by default. repair_subtitles also repairs an existing document without rerunning recognition or discarding manual speech edits. The same operation is available through the editor button Repair reading time and overlaps and via MCP/CLI. All controls are in Segmentation & layout and Advanced operations, and participate in configuration save/load.

Defaults: target 22 characters/second and 0.8 s display; at most 0.25 s advance, 0.5 s onset delay, 2 s end extension, and a 40 ms speech-caption gap. Short, fast or overlapping fragments can merge if the result fits the chosen line count and duration. Environmental-sound captions stay unchanged. The original word evidence is retained byte-for-byte as JSON data. Repeated repairs use persistent timing anchors to avoid accumulating drift; an explicit manual edit establishes a new anchor for that edited cue.

An isolated, bounded SciPy/HiGHS worker allocates reading time while respecting synchronization and media-end limits. Remaining reading-speed violations are reported rather than hidden by shifting text farther from the voice. Constraints can be adjusted explicitly. If automatic postprocessing cannot satisfy the constraints, transcription still publishes its raw result with a visible unresolved repair record; an explicit repair fails without changing its source file. No generic forced alignment or corrected transcription accuracy is claimed.

A long-form French recording was repaired through real MCP in about 2.3 seconds without rerunning its 10-minute transcription: 629 cues -> 561, 102 reading-speed warnings -> 11, 2 overlaps -> 0. Every speech word and original word timestamp was preserved. The 11 remaining fast-dialogue cues require human review/condensed wording or an explicitly wider synchronization budget. The source recording and generated artifacts are not part of the distribution.

Optional speaker diarization (0.5.0)#

Community-1 attributes speech to anonymous speaker IDs. Phonon still supplies the text and original word timestamps. Enable Identify different speakers in generation, or open an existing JSON document in the editor and use Speakers → Identify speakers in this document. The editor lets you rename people and override the speaker of individual captions. Names are display labels; the software does not discover real identities or identify a person across unrelated recordings.

In Installation, scroll to Speaker identification · Community-1. Install the optional CPU runtime, open the official model page, accept its Hugging Face conditions, then download the model. An existing Hugging Face login is reused. On Windows, a read token can alternatively be stored in Windows Credential Manager; never put tokens in MCP parameters, generation JSON or chat. The isolated runtime and weights are downloaded separately; they do not enlarge the base package or replace Phonon's PyTorch libraries.

Generation options include a known speaker count (0 = automatic), minimum/maximum count, CPU threads, segmentation and embedding batch sizes, and a duration refusal limit of at most four hours. The waveform uses job-owned disk storage and model inference uses bounded batches. This limit does not certify accuracy, processing speed or memory use for every recording. Voices are analyzed globally rather than independently renumbered for each Phonon window.

Existing-document analysis preserves manual text, times, sound captions and original words by default. Rebuild captions at speaker changes explicitly recreates speech from original words and can replace manual speech edits; sound captions remain. Timing repair does not merge different speakers. Manual speaker overrides survive re-analysis unless replacement is explicitly requested. Speaker labels can be hidden; visible names count towards reading-speed checks. A caption spanning multiple voices remains reviewable.

The JSON document remains schemaVersion 1 with additive optional speakers, diarization, speakerLabels and per-cue attribution metadata. Exported SRT/VTT can include a plain [Name] prefix compatible with ordinary players; raw cue text and original words are stored unchanged. Speaker IDs are scoped to the analyzed recording.

CLI/MCP operations: diarization_status, check_diarization_access, install_diarization_runtime, install_diarization_model, register_diarization_model, diarize_subtitles, and rename_speakers. Network installation/access operations require an authenticated network permission and install operations require explicit license review. Local model registration references an official compatible Community-1 bundle in place and hashes its files. All file inputs are automatically imported privately; export wanted outputs before FinishTask.

Community-1 uses CPU/Windows. NVIDIA CUDA is provided by the separate component below. Speaker voiceprints, arbitrary diarization architectures and automatic person naming are not exposed. The optional pipeline's own telemetry is disabled. See Diarization for the precise validation state.

NVIDIA Nemotron 3 (0.6.0)#

Install this optional engine separately in Installation after reviewing and explicitly accepting its runtime/model licenses. Select NVIDIA in the workspace, generation settings or editor Speakers panel, then choose CPU or CUDA. Phonon words/timestamps are unchanged. Voice identities are scoped to the engine and recording; switching engines does not reuse manually named identities silently.

Operations: nemotron_status, nemotron_diagnostics, install_nemotron_runtime, install_nemotron_model, register_nemotron_model. Use diarization_engine: "nemotron3" with transcribe or diarize_subtitles. Installation requires authenticated network permission and license_accepted: true; defaults do not accept terms. Both the selected runtime and the official pinned Q8_0 GGUF must be ready. Existing local weights can be referenced without moving them.

All NVIDIA mode, preset, custom geometry, segmentation and device fields are exposed through generation settings/configuration and the operation schemas. Community-1 count/batch settings must remain at their default values when using NVIDIA. A configuration load never starts inference. NvidiaDiarization.md describes limits, output metadata and evidence.

Modular CyUI interface (0.7.0)#

The subtitle timeline now uses the shared CyUI Timeline module: seek on the ruler, zoom with the wheel, pan with Shift+wheel, scroll voice lanes with Ctrl+wheel and drag clips/edges to move/trim. Escape cancels a gesture. The common Inspector validates caption drafts; Apply creates one correction. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (Ctrl+Shift+Z) restores document versions outside text entry. Ctrl+Shift+P opens the command palette.

Video preview uses CyUI Images with fit/zoom/pan. Diagnostics adds severity/search/follow and copy-visible controls while retaining full selectable log text and full-file copy. Advanced operations uses the shared JSON editor/syntax viewer. Existing business parameters, word evidence, model installations and MCP contracts are preserved. English/French, five themes and both densities remain available. See migration details and validation.

CyUI 1.2.0 uses the MIT license from the CyUI repository. The repository is currently private; the complete notice is included in LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt. The application remains AGPL-3.0-only.
pages.text: CyTools_Subtitle 0.7.0 # Local Phonon subtitles, word timing, native audio/video preview, cue editor and MCP API. Built with the actual CyToolsCore 0.10.1 MIT wheel, without copying its runtime sources. No media, UI or ML imports enter the Core. Desktop # Version 0.5.1 keeps separately timestamped punctuation with its words and handles small ASR/voice-boundary offsets when laying out captions. Ambiguous word-boundary changes use nearby phrase context; original word timestamps and raw model timelines are retained. This improves caption segmentation and does not guarantee correct speaker clustering or transcription. Version 0.4.1 fixes preview of videos with padded RGB rows, including arbitrary capture widths. Drop an audio/video file anywhere on the main window to load its preview; a subtitle JSON document can also be dropped. Invalid files show an error without closing the application. The CyUI interface provides a sidebar workspace, resizable preview/inspector columns, caption search and a separate cue editor. Options offers five semantic themes, compact/comfortable density and persistent text size; legacy dark/light/classic preferences migrate automatically. English is the default; French remains selectable. Shortcuts: Ctrl+O media, Ctrl+Shift+O subtitle JSON, Ctrl+R reload preview, Space play/pause, Left arrow back two seconds and Ctrl+S save a new subtitle bundle. Shortcuts do not intercept text entry. The Windows portable release includes Python and media/UI dependencies; PyTorch is downloaded separately from Installation: extract the complete archive, then launch ../CyTools_Subtitle.exe. Source checkouts require install.ps1 first. English is the default; French is selectable in Options. Select an audio/video source and Generate subtitles. The player streams decoding off the UI thread, overlays active captions and supports pause/seek. Source and preview pixel dimensions are displayed. The editor changes individual cue text/start/end, shifts the track, adds sound captions and exports SRT/VTT/JSON. Reflow explicitly rebuilds speech from original word timings, replacing manual speech edits while preserving sound captions. Phonon-2 and Phonon-2.5 English: English only. Phonon-2.5: multilingual, including French. Phonon does not translate or classify background sounds. Speaker attribution is available through optional Community-1 (CPU) or NVIDIA Nemotron 3 (CPU/CUDA) components. Phonon transcription remains CPU-only; NVIDIA device selection applies to voice analysis. LoRA is unsupported. Voice filtering is highpass/lowpass plus FFT denoise, not neural vocal separation. The model receives sequential bounded WAV windows, with overlap and word-midpoint ownership at boundaries. A window is deleted/reused rather than accumulating complete recording tensors. Transcription errors and boundary omissions/repetitions remain possible: review the result. Decoder timing uses native frame resolution; no timing precision or transcript completeness guarantee. Truncated inference fails explicitly and requests shorter windows. Operations # transcribe: media, model/local directory, CPU threads, audio track, windows/overlap, filter, hotwords/strength and cue layout. inspect_media: source stream metadata, dimensions and optional bounded WAV excerpt/waveform. read_subtitles: paginated original words and current cues in a time range. edit_subtitles: stable-ID text/timing patches, delete/add cues, sound descriptions and global offset. Writes a new bundle. reflow_subtitles: rebuild speech cues from the original word timing evidence. runtime_status / install_runtime: inspect or download/repair the optional pinned CPU PyTorch component, with explicit license review and authenticated network permission. model_status / install_model / register_local_model: verify, download/repair and reference compatible local models. installation_storage_status: SDK cache and Toolkit diagnostics. All declared parameters and invocation envelopes are accessible in Advanced operations, with validation, estimation, priorities and deadlines. The manifest is the common contract for standalone/CLI/MCP/HTTP. Estimates are conservative envelopes, not measured upper-bound guarantees. CLI and MCP # From the Tool root on Windows: powershell Copy .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py describe .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py describe-operation transcribe .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py --data-dir .\data\cli invoke transcribe --params-file .\app\params.json --timeout 3600 .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py --data-dir .\data\mcp mcp Replace the example media path in params.json. MCP configuration example: mcp-config.example.json. Run the private Python with app/make_mcp_config.py to print the absolute paths for your installation. Operation calls have a parameters envelope, for example op_transcribe with {"parameters":{"media":"D:/clips/example.mp4","model":"phonon-2.5"}}. Poll cy_get_job until Completed; errors/cancellation are terminal outcomes requiring review. Inspect the operation output schema before chaining outputs. AI workflow: op_inspect_media -> op_transcribe -> op_read_subtitles -> op_edit_subtitles -> cy_export_job -> cy_finish_task. Inspect audio excerpts with an audio-capable model or a classifier before adding sound descriptions. A cue with kind=sound is reviewer-supplied, not a Phonon detection. Times use seconds from the media start. JSON retains original words, chunks, source dimensions, settings and reading-speed/overlap warnings. Absolute local paths are automatically privately imported, including spaces/Unicode. No manual input copies. Original files stay intact. MCP tasks are temporary: FinishTask/disconnect removes task imports and workspaces after real workers stop. Export wanted results first. Desktop and CLI invoke sessions explicitly retain outputs. Independent MCP processes have separate queues; use authenticated shared HTTP/bridge when sharing one scheduler. Clients cannot read another client's private artifacts. Paths refer to the Tool host. Install operations require the authenticated network permission and explicit public model license review. Provision a credential using create-client --name installer --permission network, then pass the token through the local CYTOOLS_TOKEN environment or authenticated transport. No tokens in parameters, recipes or Git. Installation / updates # The local runtime uses the real wheel in app/packages. install.ps1 creates a private venv at its final path using Python 3.11, then installs the pinned Windows base requirements without PyTorch. Install PyTorch through Installation before inference. The full requirements.txt remains available for development environments. install.sh is provided for Linux but unvalidated. Local venvs are not portable; model weights and environments are excluded from source releases. Model catalog pins are copied from fermion-research==0.2.14 into model-catalog.json. The upstream downloader verifies archive hashes and supports retries; the Tool additionally hashes the local container against packed_manifest.json. Repair preserves damaged managed weights in a neighbouring .invalid-* directory. References require config.json, packed_manifest.json and matching model.fermion for the Phonon-2 family. No LoRA. Configurations contain only references, never weights/secrets. Changing shared cache settings never moves models, Python, PyTorch libraries or the system driver. Updates requires a configured owner/repository. Expected latest-release assets: cytools-app.zip and cytools-app.zip.sha256. Only confined app/ files are accepted; Tool ID, runtime ABI, platform, SHA256, size/count limits and Python syntax are checked. Dependencies remain fixed; new dependencies require a separately tested runtime. Activation at restart preserves a previous app for rollback, with data/ and runtime/ untouched. Co-published checksums are not independent signatures. No public application repository is configured; update tests use local fixtures. Verification and licenses # Private Python: -m pytest app/test_tool.py -q. app/validate_delivery.py runs actual video transcription through MCP, corrections/reflow/export/FinishTask, native audio/video playback and seek, and real cancellation. It requires local validation samples, installed models and an audio device. Evidence: data/reports/. Details: Docs/CapabilityCoverage.md and Docs/Validation.md. Copyright (c) 2026 Cyberalien. CyTools_Subtitle is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 only (AGPL-3.0-only); see LICENSE for the complete terms. The CyToolsCore SDK remains MIT. Windows x64 validated locally. Linux/macOS Unknown. Component declarations and full installed notices: licenses.json, LICENCES/, LICENSE and LICENSE-CyToolsCore.txt. Model weights keep CC-BY-4.0; the Phonon runtime keeps Apache-2.0; FFmpeg builds retain their GPL/LGPL obligations. Timing corrections in 0.2.0 # Generation and reflow now enable auto_timing by default. repair_subtitles also repairs an existing document without rerunning recognition or discarding manual speech edits. The same operation is available through the editor button Repair reading time and overlaps and via MCP/CLI. All controls are in Segmentation & layout and Advanced operations, and participate in configuration save/load. Defaults: target 22 characters/second and 0.8 s display; at most 0.25 s advance, 0.5 s onset delay, 2 s end extension, and a 40 ms speech-caption gap. Short, fast or overlapping fragments can merge if the result fits the chosen line count and duration. Environmental-sound captions stay unchanged. The original word evidence is retained byte-for-byte as JSON data. Repeated repairs use persistent timing anchors to avoid accumulating drift; an explicit manual edit establishes a new anchor for that edited cue. An isolated, bounded SciPy/HiGHS worker allocates reading time while respecting synchronization and media-end limits. Remaining reading-speed violations are reported rather than hidden by shifting text farther from the voice. Constraints can be adjusted explicitly. If automatic postprocessing cannot satisfy the constraints, transcription still publishes its raw result with a visible unresolved repair record; an explicit repair fails without changing its source file. No generic forced alignment or corrected transcription accuracy is claimed. A long-form French recording was repaired through real MCP in about 2.3 seconds without rerunning its 10-minute transcription: 629 cues -> 561, 102 reading-speed warnings -> 11, 2 overlaps -> 0. Every speech word and original word timestamp was preserved. The 11 remaining fast-dialogue cues require human review/condensed wording or an explicitly wider synchronization budget. The source recording and generated artifacts are not part of the distribution. Optional speaker diarization (0.5.0) # Community-1 attributes speech to anonymous speaker IDs. Phonon still supplies the text and original word timestamps. Enable Identify different speakers in generation, or open an existing JSON document in the editor and use Speakers → Identify speakers in this document . The editor lets you rename people and override the speaker of individual captions. Names are display labels; the software does not discover real identities or identify a person across unrelated recordings. In Installation , scroll to Speaker identification · Community-1 . Install the optional CPU runtime, open the official model page, accept its Hugging Face conditions, then download the model. An existing Hugging Face login is reused. On Windows, a read token can alternatively be stored in Windows Credential Manager; never put tokens in MCP parameters, generation JSON or chat. The isolated runtime and weights are downloaded separately; they do not enlarge the base package or replace Phonon's PyTorch libraries. Generation options include a known speaker count (0 = automatic), minimum/maximum count, CPU threads, segmentation and embedding batch sizes, and a duration refusal limit of at most four hours. The waveform uses job-owned disk storage and model inference uses bounded batches. This limit does not certify accuracy, processing speed or memory use for every recording. Voices are analyzed globally rather than independently renumbered for each Phonon window. Existing-document analysis preserves manual text, times, sound captions and original words by default. Rebuild captions at speaker changes explicitly recreates speech from original words and can replace manual speech edits; sound captions remain. Timing repair does not merge different speakers. Manual speaker overrides survive re-analysis unless replacement is explicitly requested. Speaker labels can be hidden; visible names count towards reading-speed checks. A caption spanning multiple voices remains reviewable. The JSON document remains schemaVersion 1 with additive optional speakers , diarization , speakerLabels and per-cue attribution metadata. Exported SRT/VTT can include a plain [Name] prefix compatible with ordinary players; raw cue text and original words are stored unchanged. Speaker IDs are scoped to the analyzed recording. CLI/MCP operations: diarization_status , check_diarization_access , install_diarization_runtime , install_diarization_model , register_diarization_model , diarize_subtitles , and rename_speakers . Network installation/access operations require an authenticated network permission and install operations require explicit license review. Local model registration references an official compatible Community-1 bundle in place and hashes its files. All file inputs are automatically imported privately; export wanted outputs before FinishTask. Community-1 uses CPU/Windows. NVIDIA CUDA is provided by the separate component below. Speaker voiceprints, arbitrary diarization architectures and automatic person naming are not exposed. The optional pipeline's own telemetry is disabled. See Diarization for the precise validation state. NVIDIA Nemotron 3 (0.6.0) # Install this optional engine separately in Installation after reviewing and explicitly accepting its runtime/model licenses. Select NVIDIA in the workspace, generation settings or editor Speakers panel, then choose CPU or CUDA. Phonon words/timestamps are unchanged. Voice identities are scoped to the engine and recording; switching engines does not reuse manually named identities silently. Operations: nemotron_status , nemotron_diagnostics , install_nemotron_runtime , install_nemotron_model , register_nemotron_model . Use diarization_engine: "nemotron3" with transcribe or diarize_subtitles . Installation requires authenticated network permission and license_accepted: true ; defaults do not accept terms. Both the selected runtime and the official pinned Q8_0 GGUF must be ready. Existing local weights can be referenced without moving them. All NVIDIA mode, preset, custom geometry, segmentation and device fields are exposed through generation settings/configuration and the operation schemas. Community-1 count/batch settings must remain at their default values when using NVIDIA. A configuration load never starts inference. NvidiaDiarization.md describes limits, output metadata and evidence. pages.html:
CyTools_Subtitle#

Local subtitle generation from audio and video, with a Dear ImGui media player, cue editor, and MCP/CLI API.

Français · Detailed guide · Capabilities

Features#

  • Phonon-2 for English; Phonon-2.5 for multilingual transcription, including French.
  • Sequential bounded audio windows and native word timestamps.
  • Phrase-based SRT, WebVTT and editable JSON subtitles.
  • Audio/video playback with caption overlays, pause and seek.
  • Cue text/timing edits, track offset and reviewer-supplied sound descriptions.
  • Automatic reading-time/overlap repair with explicit synchronization limits and visible unresolved warnings.
  • The same operations through the desktop editor, MCP, CLI and authenticated HTTP service.
  • English/French UI, persistent preferences, configuration save/load, separate PyTorch/model installation and compatible local references.

Windows portable download#

For the latest published Windows build, download the portable ZIP from Releases, extract the entire archive to a writable folder, and open CyTools_Subtitle.exe. Python and the media/UI dependencies are included. No system Python installation is required. In Installation, review the PyTorch license and click Download / repair PyTorch, then review the model license and download Phonon-2 or Phonon-2.5. PyTorch and model weights are downloaded separately.

English is the default interface language; French is selectable in Options. Keep app/ and runtime/ next to the executable. Settings, models and outputs are created in data/. Private release downloads require a GitHub account with access to the repository. The in-app updater currently supports public release downloads; use the browser while this repository is private.

Windows source setup#

Python 3.11 is required. In PowerShell from this directory:

powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app/install.ps1

Open CyTools_Subtitle.exe, then use Installation to review the model license and download a model. Choose your audio/video source and Generate subtitles. Review the result in the player and export the wanted files.

The environment is created privately in runtime/python. Source checkouts exclude model weights, installed environments, caches and generated results. The source setup creates a venv and requires machine Python. The Windows portable release includes its own interpreter. PyTorch is installed separately through Installation.

CPU inference is implemented and tested on Windows x64. The Linux installer/launcher is supplied but unvalidated; Linux/macOS status remains Unknown. Phonon transcription and Community-1 run on CPU. Optional NVIDIA Nemotron 3 speaker analysis supports CPU or CUDA on Windows x64. Neural vocal separation, translation and automatic environmental-sound classification are not implemented. Voice filtering is bandpass plus FFT denoise.

MCP and CLI#

powershell
.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\make_mcp_config.py.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py describe.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py --data-dir .\data\mcp mcp

The first command prints an MCP configuration with paths for your installation. Absolute local media/document paths are imported automatically; no manual staging is required. MCP task files are temporary: export wanted results before cy_finish_task or disconnect. Desktop sessions retain their outputs.

See the operation guide for transcription, inspection, editing, timing repair, models and exports.

Development#

The actual MIT CyToolsCore 0.10.1 wheel is included in app/packages. Business contracts are in app/CyTool.json. Native launcher sources and its build script are in app/. Heavy model/media/UI dependencies remain outside the Core.

powershell
.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install pytest.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest app/test_tool.py app/test_timing.py -q.\runtime\python\Scripts\cytools.exe validate app/CyTool.json

The optional delivery integration script requires locally generated sample clips, installed models and an audio device. Test evidence and platform limits are described in Validation.

Windows release build#

Build from a Windows x64 CPython 3.11 environment with the pinned dependencies. Compile the launcher with app/build_launcher.ps1 from a Visual Studio developer prompt. Run python app/build_windows.py, validate and relocate the generated directory, then run python app/build_windows.py --package-only --directory PATH. The builder downloads the official Python embeddable package, verifies its pinned SHA256 and installs dependencies into a fresh directory using app/windows-constraints.txt and app/requirements-base-windows.txt. PyTorch, SymPy, NetworkX and mpmath are excluded from the base ZIP and installed privately on request. It does not copy an existing venv. app/build_release.py builds the app update and corresponding application source archives.

Optional PyTorch runtime#

The base application opens without PyTorch: preview, subtitle editing and timing repair remain available. In Installation, review the PyTorch license and use Download / repair PyTorch. This installs pinned CPU PyTorch and its specific math dependencies into a private component directory. A new candidate is verified before activation; a failed or cancelled download does not replace an existing active component. Model files and CUDA/system drivers are not moved.

MCP/CLI clients use runtime_status and install_runtime. Installation requires the authenticated network permission and license_accepted: true; repair: true builds a new candidate. See Runtime installation. PyTorch is checked before inference and missing prerequisites produce an actionable error.

The 0.3.0 base runtime uses a new update ABI. For a 0.2.x installation, extract the new full Windows ZIP into a separate directory. Existing Phonon model folders can be referenced through Installation without moving them; keep existing data and results.

CyUI desktop#

Version 0.4.1 fixes a video preview crash on captures with padded RGB image rows. Drag an audio/video file or subtitle JSON document from the file manager onto the main window to open it. Preview decoding remains bounded and runs off the UI thread.

Version 0.4.0 uses CyUI with a sidebar, synchronized player, searchable phrase captions and an inspector for edits. Choose Mid Grey, Light Grey, Amber Night, Violet or Navy in Options, with compact/comfortable density and text scaling. English remains the default, with French selectable. PyTorch and models are still separate downloads.

CyUI is MIT-licensed by Cyberalien: official license. Its full notice is included in LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt, including for users without access to the currently private CyUI repository. Application code remains AGPL-3.0-only. The selected unmodified Python modules and their pinned revision/hashes are documented in app/cyui-source.json.

License#

Copyright (c) 2026 Cyberalien. CyTools_Subtitle is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 only (AGPL-3.0-only). The bundled CyToolsCore SDK remains MIT. Engines, libraries and model weights retain their separate licenses, including Apache-2.0, CC-BY-4.0 and the relevant FFmpeg build licenses. See LICENSE, LICENCES and app/LICENCES.

Optional speaker diarization (0.5.0+)#

Community-1 attributes speech to anonymous speaker IDs. Phonon still supplies the text and original word timestamps. Enable Identify different speakers in generation, or open an existing JSON document in the editor and use Speakers → Identify speakers in this document. The editor lets you rename people and override the speaker of individual captions. Names are display labels; the software does not discover real identities or identify a person across unrelated recordings.

In Installation, scroll to Speaker identification · Community-1. Install the optional CPU runtime, open the official model page, accept its Hugging Face conditions, then download the model. An existing Hugging Face login is reused. On Windows, a read token can alternatively be stored in Windows Credential Manager; never put tokens in MCP parameters, generation JSON or chat. The isolated runtime and weights are downloaded separately; they do not enlarge the base package or replace Phonon's PyTorch libraries.

Generation options include a known speaker count (0 = automatic), minimum/maximum count, CPU threads, segmentation and embedding batch sizes, and a duration refusal limit of at most four hours. The waveform uses job-owned disk storage and model inference uses bounded batches. This limit does not certify accuracy, processing speed or memory use for every recording. Voices are analyzed globally rather than independently renumbered for each Phonon window.

Existing-document analysis preserves manual text, times, sound captions and original words by default. Rebuild captions at speaker changes explicitly recreates speech from original words and can replace manual speech edits; sound captions remain. Timing repair does not merge different speakers. Manual speaker overrides survive re-analysis unless replacement is explicitly requested. Speaker labels can be hidden; visible names count towards reading-speed checks. A caption spanning multiple voices remains reviewable.

The JSON document remains schemaVersion 1 with additive optional speakers, diarization, speakerLabels and per-cue attribution metadata. Exported SRT/VTT can include a plain [Name] prefix compatible with ordinary players; raw cue text and original words are stored unchanged. Speaker IDs are scoped to the analyzed recording.

CLI/MCP operations: diarization_status, check_diarization_access, install_diarization_runtime, install_diarization_model, register_diarization_model, diarize_subtitles, and rename_speakers. Network installation/access operations require an authenticated network permission and install operations require explicit license review. Local model registration references an official compatible Community-1 bundle in place and hashes its files. All file inputs are automatically imported privately; export wanted outputs before FinishTask.

Community-1 uses the CPU/Windows path. NVIDIA CUDA is available through the separate optional engine below. Speaker voiceprints, arbitrary diarization architectures and automatic person naming are not exposed. The optional pipeline's own telemetry is disabled. See Diarization for the precise validation state.

Version 0.5.1 fixes punctuation-only captions and spurious word-boundary splits introduced by small ASR/voice timestamp differences. Original word timestamps and raw neural timelines remain unchanged; speaker/transcription mistakes still need review.

Optional NVIDIA speaker analysis (0.6.0)#

In Installation, open Speaker identification · NVIDIA Nemotron 3, review the separate OpenMDW 1.1 model and Apache 2.0 runtime licenses, then install the CPU or CUDA runtime and model. Downloads are separate from the base ZIP: approximately 6 MB for CPU or 102 MB for CUDA, plus a 107 MB Q8_0 model. No additional Python/PyTorch installation is needed for this engine.

Enable Identify different speakers, select NVIDIA Nemotron 3, then CPU or CUDA. This changes voice attribution; Phonon still transcribes and supplies word timestamps. The default chunked quality preset retains global voice state; full attention is limited to six minutes. NVIDIA detects up to eight anonymous voices automatically. The settings and native segmentation thresholds are also available through MCP and versioned generation configurations.

The editor shows the actual voice-analysis device and unassigned captions. Changing models creates new anonymous identities; replacing existing manual speaker assignments requires an explicit choice. Existing text and times remain intact unless caption rebuilding is requested. See NVIDIA installation, options and limits and validation evidence. The tested natural dialogue showed better main-turn separation, with some speech still unassigned; no general quality guarantee is implied.

Modular CyUI interface (0.7.0)#

The subtitle timeline now uses the shared CyUI Timeline module: seek on the ruler, zoom with the wheel, pan with Shift+wheel, scroll voice lanes with Ctrl+wheel and drag clips/edges to move/trim. Escape cancels a gesture. The common Inspector validates caption drafts; Apply creates one correction. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (Ctrl+Shift+Z) restores document versions outside text entry. Ctrl+Shift+P opens the command palette.

Video preview uses CyUI Images with fit/zoom/pan. Diagnostics adds severity/search/follow and copy-visible controls while retaining full selectable log text and full-file copy. Advanced operations uses the shared JSON editor/syntax viewer. Existing business parameters, word evidence, model installations and MCP contracts are preserved. English/French, five themes and both densities remain available. See migration details and validation.

CyUI: MIT. Full license: LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt. Upstream license: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI/blob/main/LICENSE Repository: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI (currently private; no upstream access required to run this application).

Local documentation#

Open Options → Open local manual (F1) or press F1 in the application. The complete offline reader is shipped in app/help/index.html. Regenerate the manual.

Heavy model/media/UI dependencies remain outside the Core. powershell Copy .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install pytest .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest app/test_tool.py app/test_timing.py -q .\runtime\python\Scripts\cytools.exe validate app/CyTool.json The optional delivery integration script requires locally generated sample clips, installed models and an audio device. Test evidence and platform limits are described in Validation . Windows release build # Build from a Windows x64 CPython 3.11 environment with the pinned dependencies. Compile the launcher with app/build_launcher.ps1 from a Visual Studio developer prompt. Run python app/build_windows.py , validate and relocate the generated directory, then run python app/build_windows.py --package-only --directory PATH . The builder downloads the official Python embeddable package, verifies its pinned SHA256 and installs dependencies into a fresh directory using app/windows-constraints.txt and app/requirements-base-windows.txt . PyTorch, SymPy, NetworkX and mpmath are excluded from the base ZIP and installed privately on request. It does not copy an existing venv. app/build_release.py builds the app update and corresponding application source archives. Optional PyTorch runtime # The base application opens without PyTorch: preview, subtitle editing and timing repair remain available. In Installation, review the PyTorch license and use Download / repair PyTorch . This installs pinned CPU PyTorch and its specific math dependencies into a private component directory. A new candidate is verified before activation; a failed or cancelled download does not replace an existing active component. Model files and CUDA/system drivers are not moved. MCP/CLI clients use runtime_status and install_runtime . Installation requires the authenticated network permission and license_accepted: true ; repair: true builds a new candidate. See Runtime installation . PyTorch is checked before inference and missing prerequisites produce an actionable error. The 0.3.0 base runtime uses a new update ABI. For a 0.2.x installation, extract the new full Windows ZIP into a separate directory. Existing Phonon model folders can be referenced through Installation without moving them; keep existing data and results. CyUI desktop # Version 0.4.1 fixes a video preview crash on captures with padded RGB image rows. Drag an audio/video file or subtitle JSON document from the file manager onto the main window to open it. Preview decoding remains bounded and runs off the UI thread. Version 0.4.0 uses CyUI with a sidebar, synchronized player, searchable phrase captions and an inspector for edits. Choose Mid Grey, Light Grey, Amber Night, Violet or Navy in Options, with compact/comfortable density and text scaling. English remains the default, with French selectable. PyTorch and models are still separate downloads. CyUI is MIT-licensed by Cyberalien: official license . Its full notice is included in LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt , including for users without access to the currently private CyUI repository. Application code remains AGPL-3.0-only. The selected unmodified Python modules and their pinned revision/hashes are documented in app/cyui-source.json. License # Copyright (c) 2026 Cyberalien. CyTools_Subtitle is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 only (AGPL-3.0-only). The bundled CyToolsCore SDK remains MIT. Engines, libraries and model weights retain their separate licenses, including Apache-2.0, CC-BY-4.0 and the relevant FFmpeg build licenses. See LICENSE , LICENCES and app/LICENCES. Optional speaker diarization (0.5.0+) # Community-1 attributes speech to anonymous speaker IDs. Phonon still supplies the text and original word timestamps. Enable Identify different speakers in generation, or open an existing JSON document in the editor and use Speakers → Identify speakers in this document . The editor lets you rename people and override the speaker of individual captions. Names are display labels; the software does not discover real identities or identify a person across unrelated recordings. In Installation , scroll to Speaker identification · Community-1 . Install the optional CPU runtime, open the official model page, accept its Hugging Face conditions, then download the model. An existing Hugging Face login is reused. On Windows, a read token can alternatively be stored in Windows Credential Manager; never put tokens in MCP parameters, generation JSON or chat. The isolated runtime and weights are downloaded separately; they do not enlarge the base package or replace Phonon's PyTorch libraries. Generation options include a known speaker count (0 = automatic), minimum/maximum count, CPU threads, segmentation and embedding batch sizes, and a duration refusal limit of at most four hours. The waveform uses job-owned disk storage and model inference uses bounded batches. This limit does not certify accuracy, processing speed or memory use for every recording. Voices are analyzed globally rather than independently renumbered for each Phonon window. Existing-document analysis preserves manual text, times, sound captions and original words by default. Rebuild captions at speaker changes explicitly recreates speech from original words and can replace manual speech edits; sound captions remain. Timing repair does not merge different speakers. Manual speaker overrides survive re-analysis unless replacement is explicitly requested. Speaker labels can be hidden; visible names count towards reading-speed checks. A caption spanning multiple voices remains reviewable. The JSON document remains schemaVersion 1 with additive optional speakers , diarization , speakerLabels and per-cue attribution metadata. Exported SRT/VTT can include a plain [Name] prefix compatible with ordinary players; raw cue text and original words are stored unchanged. Speaker IDs are scoped to the analyzed recording. CLI/MCP operations: diarization_status , check_diarization_access , install_diarization_runtime , install_diarization_model , register_diarization_model , diarize_subtitles , and rename_speakers . Network installation/access operations require an authenticated network permission and install operations require explicit license review. Local model registration references an official compatible Community-1 bundle in place and hashes its files. All file inputs are automatically imported privately; export wanted outputs before FinishTask. Community-1 uses the CPU/Windows path. NVIDIA CUDA is available through the separate optional engine below. Speaker voiceprints, arbitrary diarization architectures and automatic person naming are not exposed. The optional pipeline's own telemetry is disabled. See Diarization for the precise validation state. Version 0.5.1 fixes punctuation-only captions and spurious word-boundary splits introduced by small ASR/voice timestamp differences. Original word timestamps and raw neural timelines remain unchanged; speaker/transcription mistakes still need review. Optional NVIDIA speaker analysis (0.6.0) # In Installation , open Speaker identification · NVIDIA Nemotron 3 , review the separate OpenMDW 1.1 model and Apache 2.0 runtime licenses, then install the CPU or CUDA runtime and model. Downloads are separate from the base ZIP: approximately 6 MB for CPU or 102 MB for CUDA, plus a 107 MB Q8_0 model. No additional Python/PyTorch installation is needed for this engine. Enable Identify different speakers , select NVIDIA Nemotron 3 , then CPU or CUDA. This changes voice attribution; Phonon still transcribes and supplies word timestamps. The default chunked quality preset retains global voice state; full attention is limited to six minutes. NVIDIA detects up to eight anonymous voices automatically. The settings and native segmentation thresholds are also available through MCP and versioned generation configurations. The editor shows the actual voice-analysis device and unassigned captions. Changing models creates new anonymous identities; replacing existing manual speaker assignments requires an explicit choice. Existing text and times remain intact unless caption rebuilding is requested. See NVIDIA installation, options and limits and validation evidence . The tested natural dialogue showed better main-turn separation, with some speech still unassigned; no general quality guarantee is implied. Modular CyUI interface (0.7.0) # The subtitle timeline now uses the shared CyUI Timeline module: seek on the ruler, zoom with the wheel, pan with Shift+wheel, scroll voice lanes with Ctrl+wheel and drag clips/edges to move/trim. Escape cancels a gesture. The common Inspector validates caption drafts; Apply creates one correction. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (Ctrl+Shift+Z) restores document versions outside text entry. Ctrl+Shift+P opens the command palette. Video preview uses CyUI Images with fit/zoom/pan. Diagnostics adds severity/search/follow and copy-visible controls while retaining full selectable log text and full-file copy. Advanced operations uses the shared JSON editor/syntax viewer. Existing business parameters, word evidence, model installations and MCP contracts are preserved. English/French, five themes and both densities remain available. See migration details and validation . CyUI: MIT. Full license: LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt. Upstream license: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI/blob/main/LICENSE Repository: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI (currently private; no upstream access required to run this application). Local documentation # Open Options → Open local manual (F1) or press F1 in the application. The complete offline reader is shipped in app/help/index.html . Regenerate the manual . powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File app/install.ps1 .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\make_mcp_config.py .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py describe .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe .\app\tool.py --data-dir .\data\mcp mcp .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install pytest .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest app/test_tool.py app/test_timing.py -q .\runtime\python\Scripts\cytools.exe validate app/CyTool.json

# Créer un CyTool avec une IA Ce document est le contrat de travail à fournir à une IA chargée de créer un Tool.Il s'applique à Codex, Claude, OpenCode ou tout autre assistant, sans dépendance au client. ## Résultat attendu Lire [StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md](StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md) : journalsélectionnable/copiable, pixels vidéo visibles, bibliothèque de dérivés, LoRA compatibleset sélection CPU/GPU réelle, enregistrés dans les configurations de génération. Pour les Tools de maillage (génération, remesh, PBR, UV, rig), lire[MeshViewer.md](MeshViewer.md) : utiliser `--desktop --mesh-viewer` et fournir leviewport interactif avec résultat automatique, caméra libre/orbitale et éclairage. Interface anglaise par defaut, francaise en option. Lire [Localization.md](Localization.md) :onglet Options, preferences persistantes, theme/taille du texte et licences de chaque composant.Lire [SharedInstallation.md](SharedInstallation.md) : cache local/partagé configurable,CUDA Toolkit enregistré et sélectionné explicitement, Python privé et installationguidée des composants absents, avec états d'accès structurés utilisables par une IA. Une application autonome avec interface **Dear ImGui obligatoire**, un vrai lanceurWindows `.exe`, un lanceur Linux adapté et une racine rangée `app/data/runtime`.Le manifeste et les sources résident dans `app/`. Les modèles et résultats sont dans`data/`. La CLI et le MCP complètent l'interface. Lire et appliquer intégralement[StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md) : installation guidée des modèles,autorisations/licences, mises à jour GitHub, restauration et contrôles de livraison.Ne pas créer CyToolsManager et ne pas ajouter une dépendance UI au Core. ## Informations à déterminer avant l'implémentation | Information | Exemple | Emplacement ||---|---|---|| Nom et ID stable | CyToolExample / cy.tool.example | name / id || Version métier | 0.1.0 | version || Opérations | echo, convert, inspect | operations || Entrées et contraintes | text requis, steps entre 1 et 100 | inputSchema || Sorties exactes | objet avec file et mimeType | outputSchema + outputs || Exécutable externe | python, ffmpeg, programme natif | runtimeRequirements || Plateformes | Windows x64 Supported ; macOS Unknown | platforms || Backends / modèles | moteur, versions, fichiers, licences | backends[].models[] || Budget par job | RAM, VRAM par device, disque, threads CPU | resourceRequirements / estimate || Parallélisme sûr | Sequential par défaut | concurrency || Effets et accès nécessaires | network, filesystemExternal | permissions || Répertoire de données | chemin dédié au Tool/service | --data-dir || Transport | CLI seule, service partagé, pont MCP | commandes de lancement | Si une valeur est inconnue, l'écrire comme telle. Ne pas inventer une consommationVRAM, une compatibilité GPU ou un modèle installé. Les booléens de capacité décriventle code livré, pas un objectif futur. Toutes les tailles sont en **octets**, les duréesen **secondes**, la progression entre **0 et 100**. ## Procédure reproductible 1. Installer le SDK depuis le dépôt local ou le wheel fourni ; Python >= 3.11.2. Exécuter `cytools new CHEMIN --name CyToolExample --id cy.tool.example --desktop`.3. Lire les fichiers générés et conserver le point d'entrée `run_cli(create_runtime)`.4. Remplacer l'opération echo par les opérations du Tool dans `CyTool.json`.5. Implémenter un handler par opération et les enregistrer dans `create_runtime`.6. Déclarer les ressources fixes ; ajouter un estimateur si elles dépendent des paramètres.7. Isoler un runtime lourd dans `ProcessWorker` ; définir son protocole de sortie JSON.8. Ajouter des tests du comportement réel, des entrées invalides, de l'annulation,   de l'échec métier, des sorties et de l'isolation de deux clients.9. Exécuter validation du manifest, tests du Tool, CLI describe/invoke et test MCP.10. Finaliser ImGui, le parcours d'installation des modèles et les mises à jour GitHub.11. Compiler/packager les lanceurs ; ranger la distribution et tester le lancement réel.12. Documenter installation, configuration, dépendances, modèles, preuves et limites. ## Contrat Python exact ```pythonfrom pathlib import Pathfrom cytools_core import Runtime, load_manifest, CyToolErrorfrom cytools_core.transports.cli import run_cli def create_runtime(data_dir, **options):    runtime = Runtime(load_manifest(Path(__file__).with_name('CyTool.json')),                      data_dir, **options)     def write_report(context, parameters):        context.cancellation.check()        path = context.path('outputs/report.txt')        path.write_text(parameters['text'], encoding='utf-8')        context.progress(100, currentStep='Written', currentStepIndex=1, stepCount=1)        return {'file': str(path), 'mimeType': 'text/plain'}     def estimate(parameters, backend, model):        # Remplacer cet exemple par une estimation conservatrice du vrai traitement.        return {'ramBytes': 1048576,                'diskBytes': len(parameters['text'].encode('utf-8'))}     runtime.register('write_report', write_report, estimate=estimate)    return runtime if __name__ == '__main__':    raise SystemExit(run_cli(create_runtime))``` Ce code exige une opération `write_report` dans le manifest. Son `inputSchema`doit contenir `text` string requis ; son `outputSchema` doit contenir `file` et`mimeType` string requis. Déclarer `supportsProgress: true`, `canCancel: true`,`canRunAsync: true`. `file` peut porter `x-cy-kind: File` pour une future UI. Le handler reçoit une copie validée des paramètres, avec les valeurs par défautappliquées. Il retourne un objet JSON conforme à outputSchema. Un retour invalidefait échouer le job avec `InvalidOutput`. Pour un échec attendu, lever`CyToolError('MissingDependency', 'Message utile', recoverable=True)`. Ne pas appeler `runtime.start()` dans la factory : le lanceur et les tests gèrentle cycle de vie. Ne pas imprimer sur stdout depuis les handlers ; utiliser`context.log(message, level='Info')`. Les opérations natives longues doivent appeler`context.cancellation.check()` régulièrement. Le Core ne peut pas interrompre de forceun thread Python ; un programme non coopératif doit être isolé dans un worker. ## Paramètres conditionnels et UI Employer JSON Schema 2020-12 : type, properties, required, default, enum, minimum,maximum, multipleOf, items, $defs/$ref locaux et if/then/else. Ne pas créer de dialectede validation concurrent. Utiliser `x-cy-kind` et `x-cy-ui` pour les informations visuelles.Exemple complet dans [Parameters.md](Parameters.md). Le format file est une annotation,pas une permission automatique de lecture d'un fichier arbitraire. ## Backends et modèles Une opération sans backend utilise `supportedBackends: []` et n'a pas besoin de modèle.Si un seul backend est déclaré pour l'opération, il est sélectionné par défaut.Avec plusieurs backends, fournir backendId explicitement. modelId est facultatif mais,si fourni, doit appartenir au backend et être installé pour une exécution locale.L'estimateur reçoit `(parameters, backend_descriptor_or_None, model_descriptor_or_None)`.Les métadonnées d'un modèle ne constituent pas son implémentation : son installation,son chargement et son exécution appartiennent à l'adaptateur du Tool. Pour 10 Gio de VRAM : `{'vramBytes': {'auto': 10 * 1024**3}}` choisit un GPU admissible ;`{'vramBytes': {'0': 6 * 1024**3, '1': 6 * 1024**3}}` réserve deux GPU.Le backend doit effectivement savoir répartir le calcul. Ne pas mettre `simulation`dans un vrai Tool : ce device appartient aux tests. ## Partage entre plusieurs clients Pour partager une file et un modèle, démarrer **un service** et connecter les clientsavec des jetons distincts. Voir [MultiClient.md](MultiClient.md). Plusieurs processusMCP autonomes lancés dans des dossiers différents ont des runtimes différents.Ne pas prétendre qu'ils partagent automatiquement leur VRAM ou leurs modèles. ## Définition de terminé Appliquer aussi tous les critères de [StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md).La génération d'un squelette ou une commande CLI réussie ne suffit pas. L'interface Dear ImGui doit respecter [Localization.md](Localization.md) : anglaispar défaut, français sélectionnable et onglet Options avec préférences et licences.Appliquer [GenerationConfigurations.md](GenerationConfigurations.md) : sauvegarde etchargement du formulaire, autosave optionnelle des paramètres soumis, JSON versionnéréutilisable par une IA et exclusion des secrets. Vérifier un aller-retour réel duformulaire et un rejeu via le runtime. Le chargement ne démarre jamais la génération. - `cytools validate CyTool.json` réussit.- La CLI décrit toutes les opérations implémentées et exécute un cas réel.- Les sorties valident outputSchema ; les chemins créés restent dans le workspace.- Un client B ne lit ni n'annule un job privé du client A.- L'annulation libère réellement le worker avant les réservations.- Un paramètre incorrect et une dépendance absente donnent un code d'erreur utile.- Le catalogue MCP est dérivé du manifest et l'appel crée un job consultable.- README donne des commandes testées et les variables d'environnement exactes.- Les plateformes testées sont distinguées des plateformes simplement déclarées. Pour un SDK natif C++/C#, reproduire le protocole et les mêmes fixtures de conformité.Une première intégration peut déjà utiliser le service HTTP ou un worker JSON stdin/stdout.Ne pas réécrire le scheduler dans chaque Tool.  Lire [FullOperationAccess.md](FullOperationAccess.md) : inventaire des capacités natives, parité complète des options métier entre IA et standalone, contrats de sorties composables et preuves de validation. Un formulaire simplifié ne limite pas le contrat du Tool. Lire Docs/AutomaticInputs.md (AutomaticInputs.md depuis Docs) : chemins absolus acceptés pour les entrées locales, copie automatique privée par job, aucune copie manuelle exigée de l’IA.  ## Task-owned files (SDK 0.9.0) Read Docs/TaskFiles.md (TaskFiles.md from this Docs directory). Configure input roots and all file fields for automatic imports; AI sessions are temporary by default. FinishTask removes imported copies and generated workspaces after workers stop; export wanted results first. Standalone sessions explicitly use temporary=False. ## Partager un GPU entre plusieurs opérations (SDK 0.10.0) Lire [Scheduler.md](Scheduler.md). Déclarer `exclusiveGroups: ["gpu"]` dans toutes lesopérations qui utilisent un même moteur non concurrent, y compris ses opérations dechargement/déchargement quand elles peuvent entrer en conflit. Configurer `concurrency`pour laisser les opérations indépendantes progresser. Ne pas créer une seconde filelocale dans les handlers ; conserver les réservations RAM/VRAM et les contraintes backend.Épingler le SDK 0.10.0 ou ultérieur et tester deux clients, une opération indépendante,les priorités, les délais, l'échec et une annulation avant l'arrêt réel du worker.Les groupes ne coordonnent pas des processus Runtime différents. Il s'applique à Codex, Claude, OpenCode ou tout autre assistant, sans dépendance au client. ## Résultat attendu Lire [StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md](StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md) : journal sélectionnable/copiable, pixels vidéo visibles, bibliothèque de dérivés, LoRA compatibles et sélection CPU/GPU réelle, enregistrés dans les configurations de génération. Pour les Tools de maillage (génération, remesh, PBR, UV, rig), lire [MeshViewer.md](MeshViewer.md) : utiliser `--desktop --mesh-viewer` et fournir le viewport interactif avec résultat automatique, caméra libre/orbitale et éclairage. Interface anglaise par defaut, francaise en option. Lire [Localization.md](Localization.md) : onglet Options, preferences persistantes, theme/taille du texte et licences de chaque composant. Lire [SharedInstallation.md](SharedInstallation.md) : cache local/partagé configurable, CUDA Toolkit enregistré et sélectionné explicitement, Python privé et installation guidée des composants absents, avec états d'accès structurés utilisables par une IA. Une application autonome avec interface **Dear ImGui obligatoire**, un vrai lanceur Windows `.exe`, un lanceur Linux adapté et une racine rangée `app/data/runtime`. Le manifeste et les sources résident dans `app/`. Les modèles et résultats sont dans `data/`. La CLI et le MCP complètent l'interface. Lire et appliquer intégralement [StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md) : installation guidée des modèles, autorisations/licences, mises à jour GitHub, restauration et contrôles de livraison. Ne pas créer CyToolsManager et ne pas ajouter une dépendance UI au Core. ## Informations à déterminer avant l'implémentation | Information | Exemple | Emplacement | |---|---|---| | Nom et ID stable | CyToolExample / cy.tool.example | name / id | | Version métier | 0.1.0 | version | | Opérations | echo, convert, inspect | operations | | Entrées et contraintes | text requis, steps entre 1 et 100 | inputSchema | | Sorties exactes | objet avec file et mimeType | outputSchema + outputs | | Exécutable externe | python, ffmpeg, programme natif | runtimeRequirements | | Plateformes | Windows x64 Supported ; macOS Unknown | platforms | | Backends / modèles | moteur, versions, fichiers, licences | backends[].models[] | | Budget par job | RAM, VRAM par device, disque, threads CPU | resourceRequirements / estimate | | Parallélisme sûr | Sequential par défaut | concurrency | | Effets et accès nécessaires | network, filesystemExternal | permissions | | Répertoire de données | chemin dédié au Tool/service | --data-dir | | Transport | CLI seule, service partagé, pont MCP | commandes de lancement | Si une valeur est inconnue, l'écrire comme telle. Ne pas inventer une consommation VRAM, une compatibilité GPU ou un modèle installé. Les booléens de capacité décrivent le code livré, pas un objectif futur. Toutes les tailles sont en **octets**, les durées en **secondes**, la progression entre **0 et 100**. ## Procédure reproductible 1. Installer le SDK depuis le dépôt local ou le wheel fourni ; Python >= 3.11. 2. Exécuter `cytools new CHEMIN --name CyToolExample --id cy.tool.example --desktop`. 3. Lire les fichiers générés et conserver le point d'entrée `run_cli(create_runtime)`. 4. Remplacer l'opération echo par les opérations du Tool dans `CyTool.json`. 5. Implémenter un handler par opération et les enregistrer dans `create_runtime`. 6. Déclarer les ressources fixes ; ajouter un estimateur si elles dépendent des paramètres. 7. Isoler un runtime lourd dans `ProcessWorker` ; définir son protocole de sortie JSON. 8. Ajouter des tests du comportement réel, des entrées invalides, de l'annulation, de l'échec métier, des sorties et de l'isolation de deux clients. 9. Exécuter validation du manifest, tests du Tool, CLI describe/invoke et test MCP. 10. Finaliser ImGui, le parcours d'installation des modèles et les mises à jour GitHub. 11. Compiler/packager les lanceurs ; ranger la distribution et tester le lancement réel. 12. Documenter installation, configuration, dépendances, modèles, preuves et limites. ## Contrat Python exact ```python from pathlib import Path from cytools_core import Runtime, load_manifest, CyToolError from cytools_core.transports.cli import run_cli def create_runtime(data_dir, **options): runtime = Runtime(load_manifest(Path(__file__).with_name('CyTool.json')), data_dir, **options) def write_report(context, parameters): context.cancellation.check() path = context.path('outputs/report.txt') path.write_text(parameters['text'], encoding='utf-8') context.progress(100, currentStep='Written', currentStepIndex=1, stepCount=1) return {'file': str(path), 'mimeType': 'text/plain'} def estimate(parameters, backend, model): # Remplacer cet exemple par une estimation conservatrice du vrai traitement. return {'ramBytes': 1048576, 'diskBytes': len(parameters['text'].encode('utf-8'))} runtime.register('write_report', write_report, estimate=estimate) return runtime if __name__ == '__main__': raise SystemExit(run_cli(create_runtime)) ``` Ce code exige une opération `write_report` dans le manifest. Son `inputSchema` doit contenir `text` string requis ; son `outputSchema` doit contenir `file` et `mimeType` string requis. Déclarer `supportsProgress: true`, `canCancel: true`, `canRunAsync: true`. `file` peut porter `x-cy-kind: File` pour une future UI. Le handler reçoit une copie validée des paramètres, avec les valeurs par défaut appliquées. Il retourne un objet JSON conforme à outputSchema. Un retour invalide fait échouer le job avec `InvalidOutput`. Pour un échec attendu, lever `CyToolError('MissingDependency', 'Message utile', recoverable=True)`. Ne pas appeler `runtime.start()` dans la factory : le lanceur et les tests gèrent le cycle de vie. Ne pas imprimer sur stdout depuis les handlers ; utiliser `context.log(message, level='Info')`. Les opérations natives longues doivent appeler `context.cancellation.check()` régulièrement. Le Core ne peut pas interrompre de force un thread Python ; un programme non coopératif doit être isolé dans un worker. ## Paramètres conditionnels et UI Employer JSON Schema 2020-12 : type, properties, required, default, enum, minimum, maximum, multipleOf, items, $defs/$ref locaux et if/then/else. Ne pas créer de dialecte de validation concurrent. Utiliser `x-cy-kind` et `x-cy-ui` pour les informations visuelles. Exemple complet dans [Parameters.md](Parameters.md). Le format file est une annotation, pas une permission automatique de lecture d'un fichier arbitraire. ## Backends et modèles Une opération sans backend utilise `supportedBackends: []` et n'a pas besoin de modèle. Si un seul backend est déclaré pour l'opération, il est sélectionné par défaut. Avec plusieurs backends, fournir backendId explicitement. modelId est facultatif mais, si fourni, doit appartenir au backend et être installé pour une exécution locale. L'estimateur reçoit `(parameters, backend_descriptor_or_None, model_descriptor_or_None)`. Les métadonnées d'un modèle ne constituent pas son implémentation : son installation, son chargement et son exécution appartiennent à l'adaptateur du Tool. Pour 10 Gio de VRAM : `{'vramBytes': {'auto': 10 * 1024**3}}` choisit un GPU admissible ; `{'vramBytes': {'0': 6 * 1024**3, '1': 6 * 1024**3}}` réserve deux GPU. Le backend doit effectivement savoir répartir le calcul. Ne pas mettre `simulation` dans un vrai Tool : ce device appartient aux tests. ## Partage entre plusieurs clients Pour partager une file et un modèle, démarrer **un service** et connecter les clients avec des jetons distincts. Voir [MultiClient.md](MultiClient.md). Plusieurs processus MCP autonomes lancés dans des dossiers différents ont des runtimes différents. Ne pas prétendre qu'ils partagent automatiquement leur VRAM ou leurs modèles. ## Définition de terminé Appliquer aussi tous les critères de [StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md). La génération d'un squelette ou une commande CLI réussie ne suffit pas. L'interface Dear ImGui doit respecter [Localization.md](Localization.md) : anglais par défaut, français sélectionnable et onglet Options avec préférences et licences. Appliquer [GenerationConfigurations.md](GenerationConfigurations.md) : sauvegarde et chargement du formulaire, autosave optionnelle des paramètres soumis, JSON versionné réutilisable par une IA et exclusion des secrets. Vérifier un aller-retour réel du formulaire et un rejeu via le runtime. Le chargement ne démarre jamais la génération. - `cytools validate CyTool.json` réussit. - La CLI décrit toutes les opérations implémentées et exécute un cas réel. - Les sorties valident outputSchema ; les chemins créés restent dans le workspace. - Un client B ne lit ni n'annule un job privé du client A. - L'annulation libère réellement le worker avant les réservations. - Un paramètre incorrect et une dépendance absente donnent un code d'erreur utile. - Le catalogue MCP est dérivé du manifest et l'appel crée un job consultable. - README donne des commandes testées et les variables d'environnement exactes. - Les plateformes testées sont distinguées des plateformes simplement déclarées. Pour un SDK natif C++/C#, reproduire le protocole et les mêmes fixtures de conformité. Une première intégration peut déjà utiliser le service HTTP ou un worker JSON stdin/stdout. Ne pas réécrire le scheduler dans chaque Tool. Lire [FullOperationAccess.md](FullOperationAccess.md) : inventaire des capacités natives, parité complète des options métier entre IA et standalone, contrats de sorties composables et preuves de validation. Un formulaire simplifié ne limite pas le contrat du Tool. Lire Docs/AutomaticInputs.md (AutomaticInputs.md depuis Docs) : chemins absolus acceptés pour les entrées locales, copie automatique privée par job, aucune copie manuelle exigée de l’IA. ## Task-owned files (SDK 0.9.0) Read Docs/TaskFiles.md (TaskFiles.md from this Docs directory). Déclarer `exclusiveGroups: ["gpu"]` dans toutes les opérations qui utilisent un même moteur non concurrent, y compris ses opérations de chargement/déchargement quand elles peuvent entrer en conflit. Configurer `concurrency` pour laisser les opérations indépendantes progresser. Ne pas créer une seconde file locale dans les handlers ; conserver les réservations RAM/VRAM et les contraintes backend. Épingler le SDK 0.10.0 ou ultérieur et tester deux clients, une opération indépendante, les priorités, les délais, l'échec et une annulation avant l'arrêt réel du worker. Les groupes ne coordonnent pas des processus Runtime différents. Licence et redistribution commerciale : lire [Licensing.md](Licensing.md).         path.write_text(parameters['text'], encoding='utf-8')
